When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Johnny Depp returning to theaters in Ebenezer on the 2026 movie schedule, renewed interest has grown in whether he'll ever play Captain Jack Sparrow again. Producer Jerry Bruckheimer has already confirmed that discussions have taken place about bringing Depp back for Pirates of the Caribbean 6, although nothing has been officially announced. Now another familiar face from the original movies has weighed in, and I have to admit, this is one reunion I'd love to see happen.

Mackenzie Crook, who played the perpetually confused Ragetti in the first three Pirates movies, recently discussed the possibility of returning to the franchise during an appearance on The Daily Beast's Obsessed podcast. The actor, who starred alongside Lee Arenberg's Pintel as one of the series' most entertaining comedic duos, hasn't appeared in a Pirates movie since 2007's At World's End. Although nearly 20 years later, he sounds more than willing to dig out that wooden eye. Crook explained:

Yes, I think I would for the hell of it. It would be so interesting – obviously it would depend on the script – to even just have a cameo to see what happened to those characters, Pintel and Ragetti, what happened to them after we last saw them. Again, I was really fond of those characters and working with Lee Arenberg, who plays Pintel. Yeah, we had a blast doing that stuff. It was great.

I would absolutely love this. Pintel and Ragetti were two of my favorite supporting characters from the original trilogy, and their ridiculous behavior provided some great comic relief between all the sword fights and increasingly more extravagant set pieces.

For anybody who needs a refresher, the pair started as members of Barbossa's cursed crew in The Curse of the Black Pearl. Ragetti was the skinny, somewhat dimwitted pirate with a wooden eye. Pintel was his considerably louder and equally incompetent partner.

Somehow, they survived three movies filled with undead pirates, sea monsters and increasingly complicated betrayals. That's honestly impressive considering how frequently they seemed to have no idea what was going on. While I certainly want to see Johnny Depp return as Jack Sparrow, I think bringing back characters like these could be just as important to making another Pirates movie feel connected to the originals.

Crook also had some interesting memories of working on the films. During the interview, he recalled the sometimes exhausting experience of shooting aboard actual ships at sea. He also discussed the rather uncomfortable process of bringing Ragetti's wooden eye to life, which required wearing two contact lenses, including one designed to create the appearance of wood grain.

Apparently, playing a pirate wasn't quite as glamorous as it looked. The actor also reflected on the amount of practical filmmaking involved in the original trilogy. Although the movies relied heavily on visual effects, Crook remembered productions where crews actually rigged ships with explosives rather than recreating everything digitally. He described those experiences as some of the last examples of old-fashioned blockbuster filmmaking.

I think that's part of what makes those first three movies so much fun to revisit with a Disney+ subscription. Even when the stories got complicated, something fantastically chaotic about watching these characters run around enormous pirate ships, usually making whatever situation they were in considerably worse. Of course, whether any of them actually return is another matter.

Bruckheimer previously confirmed that he's been speaking with Depp about a sixth movie, although the project remains in development. Depp recently suggested he'd be interested in helping give the franchise a proper sendoff, particularly if it meant working with Bruckheimer again.

Meanwhile, other original cast members have expressed interest in returning. Orlando Bloom has discussed the possibility of another Pirates movie, though there's still no indication that Will Turner will be part of whatever Disney ultimately decides to make.

That's really where we stand. There's no confirmed cast or release date for Pirates of the Caribbean 6, and Crook's comments are just an expression of interest, not evidence he's been approached.

I do like his idea of a cameo that lets audiences catch up with Pintel and Ragetti. It's been almost two decades since we last saw the two idiots, and I can't help wondering what they've been doing with themselves.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

#3630. Jan Ravnik and Maks Chmerkovskiy's DWTS Drama: Timeline

Jan Ravnik’s drama with Maks Chmerkovskiy has rocked the Dancing With the Stars fandom.

Maks criticized Jan’s first season on the show during an appearance on wife Peta Murgatroyd’s “The Penthouse With Peta” podcast.

“I’m sorry, Jan has absolutely no business being a pro on Dancing With the Stars,” Maks said during the October 2025 episode. His comments were immediately met with widespread backlash.

Maks himself was a controversial figure on the show during his 17 years as a pro. He officially retired after season 25 in 2017. Jan, meanwhile, made his debut last month alongside celebrity partner Jen Affleck, who stars on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives. (The duo were eliminated during the October 28, 2025, live show.)

In the wake of Maks’ comments, Jan and several other DWTS pros — past and present — have weighed in on the drama.

“I had so much support from production,” Jan said during the DWTS “Official Podcast” on October 30, 2025, when discussing his experience on the show. “The pros are always there. They were always cheering me up. Everyone’s so nice. It’s like a small family. I felt supported.”

Keep scrolling for a complete timeline of the Maks and Jan drama:

Maks claimed that Jan has “zero foundation technique, quality, understanding of the partnership,” during his “The Penthouse With Peta” podcast appearance on October 24, 2025.

“I’m getting emotional,” he added. “It is absurd, and this is unreal how blind we have to be and God forbid say what’s obviously there.”

Maks continued, “How are you going to expect him to teach it and deliver that message in a format that is completely different from even ballroom dancing? We had this criticism weeks ago, and I’m like, ‘Bro, is anybody going to explain it to him?’”

Jen posted a TikTok with Jan on October 27, 2025, that was captioned: “Me When Anyone Talks Trash About Jan.”

The Hulu star was furiously typing on her phone in the clip before Jan stepped in and stopped her.

“Take it down. Take it down. Take it down. We need it gone,” Jan could be seen mouthing over a TikTok audio. “That doesn’t represent me or what we need to be doing.”

While the drama wasn’t acknowledged head-on during the DWTS live show on October 28, 2025, Derek praised Jan while judging the show.

“Jan, first of all,” he said. “I want to tell you, my man, that you are doing a fantastic first season.”

Following his elimination, Jan spoke with Us exclusively and addressed the drama.

“I mean, look, everyone has [an] opinion. Everyone has a right to have [an] opinion,” he said. “Haters [are] going to hate and whoever loves us, loves us.”

Maks’ brother, Val Chmerkovskiy, addressed the situation following the DWTS live show on October 28, 2025.

“You don’t have to like what he said. I don’t have to agree with what he said. But I’m always going to stand up for him,” Val clarified. “Do I disagree with it? Yeah, completely. Do I think it’s hurtful for a current professional who is currently in the season to hear feedback like that? Of course, that’s incredibly hurtful.”

Maks’ sister-in-law, DWTS pro Jenna Johnson, shared her thoughts with Us exclusively on October 29, 2025.

“I think everyone is welcome to have their own opinion,” she said on the red carpet at Variety‘s Power of Women event. “I absolutely adore Jan.”

Maks’ wife, Peta Murgatroyd, weighed in on the resulting drama on the October 31, 2025, episode of her “Penthouse With Peta” podcast.

“Some of our critiques came off more harshly than intended. I wanted to be really clear that was never the goal,” she said. “We never want to condone hate or personal attacks of any kind. We love Dancing With the Stars. It’s one of the best shows on television, and a show that has given me so much over the years.”

Murgatroyd continued, “Jan and Rylee, please know that our intention was never to make things personal. We’re so sorry for hurting your feelings. Our goal is to discuss performances from a professional ballroom dancer’s perspective, and, unfortunately, sometimes our passion can be mistaken for negativity — but that’s never where our hearts are.”

In light of the resulting drama and backlash, Maks issued a response.

“I want to apologize to Jan for the way my words made you feel [and] for hurting your feelings,” he said in a social media video shared on October 30, 2025. “There’s a lot more that I wanted to say. I would like the opportunity to do it over coffee, or any kind of time you have to spare.”

Maks added that his dance feedback “doesn’t come with feelings and emotions.”

“It just comes with [a] completely different range of reasoning, and I’m that guy,” he stated. “I’m very honest and very black and white. It may be late in the game, but when I realize something about myself, I realize … because I finally understand that for myself.”

During the November 2026 semifinals of DWTS season 35, Jan was told during a live backstage interview that his waltz with partner Tatyana Ali was “beautiful.” He responded, “Say that to Maks,” and pointed a finger toward the camera.

#3629. Grand Theft Auto 6 Performance Is Mostly Stable, Except On Xbox Series S Where It Can Hit Sub-20FPS

With Grand Theft Auto 6âs world being as big as it is and current consoles being six years old, thereâs naturally a bit of worry about how the game performs on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Our reviewer played the game on a PS5 Pro, considered to be the most powerful console on the market right now, and said that while it runs at 30 frames-per-second most of the time, there were still some noticeable frame drops in crowded areas.

But if you havenât bought a PS5 Pro, what can you expect from GTA 6âs performance? Well, the folks over at Digital Foundry have done what they do best and created some lengthy technical breakdowns of the game, including stress testing it in explosive situations.

According to their video, the PS5 Pro tends to hold a pretty solid 30fps, unless you go around making a mess by blowing up a lot of cars at once; in those moments Digital Foundry saw the game dip to around 24fps at its lowest. The base PS5, however, seems to struggle to maintain 30fps in the best of cases, and if you decide to cause a lot of on-screen destruction, those dips are actually sustained until you leave an area.Â

On the Xbox side, the Xbox Series X seems to share the same relative stability as the PS5 Pro, with the same frame drops during car chases, crowded scenes, or firefights when things get busier on screen. The big question is how the Xbox Series S, which was originally released in 2020 as a cheaper, lower-powered alternative to the bougie, more expensive consoles of the year, handles GTA 6. According to Digital Foundry, there are some details that are less prevalent or rendered with lower-res textures, and the resolution is lower, coming in at 720p compared to the 1440p of Series X.

The DF video has a number of comparison shots demonstrating how a lot of small details have been downgraded on Series S, but the real difference is that the framerate is, unsurprisingly, struggling the most on the less powerful Xbox. Digital Foundry reports that while 30fps is the target, even the most “typical” play can affect framerate, with standard combat encounters and car chases dropping it to around 25 and the more demanding carnage bringing it down to 20. There’s even a few seconds in the video where it gets down to 18 and 19fps during an explosive shootout.

Ultimately, if youâre hoping for the smoothest possible experience, the PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X are the unsurprising winners here. A PC version of the game is rumored to launch sometime next year, and I imagine thatâs where folks with high-end builds are going to be able to get smoother, 60fps framerates as Rockstar apparently has no plans to add a Performance Mode to GTA6 on consoles. If youâre running a Series S, maybe try not to cause too much mayhem along the way for best results.Â

Though the Xbox Series S provided a more affordable way for people to jump into the next generation of gaming consoles in 2020, as time has gone on and games have gotten more demanding on the hardware, developers have expressed frustration with having to make their games compatible with the device. Tekken director Katsuhiro Harada described it as akin to âhaving to do extra work for a slightly weaker child.â

#3628. Kate Middleton Announces First Major Trip Since Her Cancer Diagnosis

In unexpected news, Kensington Palace has just announced that Kate Middleton will accompany Prince William on his upcoming three-day official visit to Mumbai, India. The trip, which commences on Monday, will mark their first joint tour outside the United Kingdom in the past four years and represents a new milestone in Kate Middleton’s gradual return to public duties since she was diagnosed with cancer in early 2024 and began scaling back her official engagements.

Last May, the princess made a brief solo trip to Italy to learn about early childhood development, but this trip to India (a nine-hour flight from London) represents her first long-distance journey and her highest-profile diplomatic engagement since the Caribbean tour she undertook in 2022 and the Earthshot Awards gala she attended in Boston that same year.

"So proud, I'm very, very proud. She's been amazing. She's been through so much in the last couple of years, particularly," William shared on UK radio show Heart Breakfast in May, pleased to see that Kate was “gradually resuming” her travels. Still, the heir to the throne wanted to be cautious and warned that these visits are very taxing. "Away trips like that take a lot out of you," he explained. "So we have to balance that, make sure she's, she's OK and rested, but she's in good form."

The royal couple at the 2022 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Boston, their most recent joint trip abroad to date

The reason for the visit is the sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize, an initiative spearheaded by the heir to the British throne that each year awards one million pounds (about $1,323,249) to five innovative environmental projects and which, after making stops in other cities abroad such as Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro, is now taking place in the country that has produced the most finalists and winners in the competition’s history.

Standout finalists this year include Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, for its fleet of electric motorcycle taxis designed to reduce urban pollution, and Mahila Housing Trust, which installs reflective roofs capable of lowering the temperature inside homes by up to five degrees during extreme heat. The awards ceremony will be held this Tuesday evening at the Jio World Centre in Mumbai and will feature a performance by the band Take That and be attended by celebrities such as actor Rami Malek.

William and Kate during their 2016 visit to the Taj Mahal

Hours before the main event, the Prince and Princess of Wales will also preside over the first edition of the Earthshot Children’s Awards, a competition in which 15,000 schools from 24 Indian states have participated with environmental proposals designed by young people aged 9 to 17. The itinerary also includes a solo appearance by Kate Middleton, meetings with the Bollywood film industry, cricket-related celebrations, and a possible meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In addition to being a positive sign regarding the princess’s health, this return to India holds strong symbolic significance for the couple, who last visited the country in April 2016. On that occasion, the then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge visited the Taj Mahal and posed on the same white marble bench where Princess Diana was photographed alone in 1992—an image that has gone down in history as a reflection of the breakdown of her marriage to the now-King Charles III.

I'm psyched for Fallout's third season whenever it comes out (Kyle MacLachlan says it could be May or June next year), but I'd be perfectly happy if it had an ending and the show was done. Better to tell your story and leave it there than drag out a show just because it's popular and end up finishing on a wet fart of a finale when you should have gone out on, er, whatever the opposite of a wet fart is.

Season 3 has finished filming, but right now not even Walton Goggins, who plays The Ghoul, is sure what the future holds for Fallout's TV incarnation. Talking about how the show's maintaining the "subversive humor and the satirical kind of elements" it brought over from the games at an awards screening attended by GamesRadar, he said, "I feel confident that we've done that in season three, and if we get the opportunity to come back for season four, that would continue to honor how sacred this is to people. It's not something that we take lightly."

Goggins as we know doesn't play videogames himself. And co-star Aaron Moten has sworn off playing Fallout, leaving Ella Purnell the only actor to roll a Vault Dweller out of the headline trio. But despite that, Goggins is still aware of what the games mean to people.

"I mean, my son is a gamer. I see exactly how and why he plays games. I'm not a gamer at all, but the game of Fallout has been around for such a long time. It's been a shared experience between parents and their children and friends for such a long time, but it holds a very special place in their heart," Goggins said.

"I think what they have responded to, at least what I've been told out on the road, is the reverence in which all of us approach the sacred nature of this game, and while still keeping it an original story in the canon of Fallout."

Fallout Season 3 will feature another definite videogame-enjoyer in its cast, though. Aaron Paul, star of Dispatch and some other stuff I guess, has joined the show 16 years after attending a launch event for Fallout: New Vegas.

We’re only a few days away from the Traitors: New Blood finale, and I’m willing to admit the obvious. This has not been the best season of The Traitors. In fact, you could easily say this has been a below-average season. Fans on social media and those I have talked to in real life seem to all be in agreement on that. There’s a growing consensus that the show needs to change. I think producers are going to listen, though I’m terrified they’re going to misunderstand the why.

The biggest, loudest and most obvious change we’ve gotten this season has been the casting of non-celebrities. The US version of The Traitors has historically relied on reality television personalities to provide the drama and bring their fanbases. This season, NBC decided to move the property from Peacock to network television and cast it like a more traditional competition show with randoms. It would be easy to just look at that decision and blame all the problems on the newbies, but that’s actually not the right takeaway.

The biggest problem by a very large margin with Traitors: New Blood is the episode runtimes. The show simply does not work in an hour-long time slot on NBC. In theory, the episodes on Peacock are the same length, as they’re typically between an hour and an hour and ten minutes. Because they’re on streaming, however, that runtime is the actual length of each episode. On network television, an hour-long time slot is actually forty-two minutes or so of real content, which isn’t even close to the amount of time the players need to complete one cycle of the game.

That means every single episode, the editors are making an impossible choice. They can either not include one or more major elements of the show (the breakfast, the mission, the roundtable and the turret), they can completely remove all of the strategy scenes that happen between those major elements, or they can drop most of the confessionals where the players talk directly to the camera and tell us their motivations and theories. There is simply no way to get through all of that in forty-two minutes. So, that has left every episode feeling either incomplete because it didn’t make it through a full cycle of the game, or feeling like a highlight video that simply recaps the basics of what happened.

That format and structure are the problem. The runtime is the problem. It’s not the cast. Even with less confessionals and less screentime, we’ve gotten good content from these players. I’m not saying the Traitors: New Blood cast is better than the cast on Big Brother 14 or Survivor: Heroes vs Villains, but there are some breakout personalities here and plenty of likeable, solid characters who have popped and would have looked even better with more of a chance to talk to the camera.

Victor is an all-time great Traitors character and should be a reality television mainstay moving forward. He’s electric. I’m personally obsessed with Jay and have had probably ten conversations with people trying to figure out his vibe and what’s going on in his head. It’s not just those two standouts either. There are a half dozen or so other players who play hard and are capable of delivering strong confessionals. Joe, Katie, Tomica, Michael and Shane have all had great moments, and when given a chance, secondary characters like Wyatt, Clyde, Abby, Abbey, Kriste, Ben, Morgan and others have delivered too. They’re just not always getting the screentime because, once again, every episode feels like it’s set on 1.5X speed.

Survivor and The Amazing Race have lengthened their episodes in recent years to help develop the characters and let the episodes breathe more. That’s the obvious solution here for The Traitors. It either needs to move to 90 minutes, or it needs to move back to Peacock. What it absolutely does not need to do is give up on casting newbies. The UK and other countries have had fantastic seasons using randoms, and in an ideal world, it would be a delight to watch Peacock/ NBC switch back and forth between a season with reality stars and a season with plumbers, farmers and firefighters.

I love The Traitors. It’s one of my favorite shows on television, and despite the obvious format issues, I still enjoyed the content we got this season. I’d like to see producers listen to the fan frustration and make a change, but those alterations should be exclusively focused on the format and not on casting.

#3625. Joe Amabile Gives 'Great' Update After MRI Amid Brain Surgery Recovery

Bachelor Nation’s Joe Amabile is offering a positive update after undergoing an MRI amid his recovery from brain surgery.

“Got my results back from my MRI. It’s clean,” Amabile, 40, shared in a Wednesday, November 18, Instagram video. “Recovering well. Surgery went great. So, I’m good to go.”

He echoed in the caption, “MRI came back clean. No signs of a tumor and my brain is recovering great.”

Days prior, Amabile opened up about feeling nervous before undergoing his MRI.

“I’ve been feeling a little out of it the past couple days, but the weather is so nice I just went for a run. My first MRI from my surgery is next week, so I’m a little worried about that. But …” Amabile said in a November 11 Instagram Story as he shrugged his shoulders.

Amabile shared in July that he was preparing to undergo brain surgery after participating in a Prenuvo full body scan, which revealed a “blueberry size lesion.” Amabile underwent surgery in August and later revealed that he had been diagnosed with a “very low grade” astrocytoma — a type of brain or spinal cord tumor that may result in headaches, seizures, nausea or changes in mood or behavior, per the Mayo Clinic.

“They did get the whole thing,” he said in his video at the time. “When it comes to malignant brain tumors, they don’t know what’s left over, so I will be going on treatment, which is just a pill every day for the rest of my life to put the bad cells to sleep, and hopefully they stay asleep.”

Amid his recovery, Amabile began training for the New York City Marathon.

“Having brain surgery is, kind of, out of your control and having a brain tumor is something that’s out of your control, so to give myself a goal that gave me control back just made me feel like it was important,” Amabile exclusively told Us in October. “I just kept my mindset positive.”

“I didn’t think I was retired from running marathons, but then I was like, ‘You know what? I’m gonna do it. I’m gonna do it again this year, three months after I had brain surgery,’” he continued. “The feeling I will get when I cross the finish line, I’m sure will be greater than both marathons, even though I’m gonna run it slower.”

Just 88 days after undergoing brain surgery, Amabile crossed the finish line in the Big Apple. His wife, Serena Pitt, cheered him on from the sidelines.

“WHAT A DAY! My worst time yet and my greatest accomplishment at the same time,” Amabile wrote via Instagram, to which Pitt, 29, commented, “I’ll never forget today. You inspire me and so many around you!!”

#3624. Sam Altman Is “Still Unknowable” to Andrew Garfield, Even After Playing the OpenAI Co-Founder in Artificial

In Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, the director follows the rise of OpenAI and a few of its pioneers: Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever and Mira Murati. The result is one of the most talked-about and timely films of the season.

“The topic is not the artificial intelligence for me, but it's the people who imagined it, who created it, who exploited it and who are still in the mix of doing all these things,” Guadagnino said during a discussion led by VF's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday. “I was very much into trying to decipher, understand this world of this new generation, let’s say tech bros, that were somehow behaving in a way that was not exactly as you could see the previous generation doing … So it was too attractive not to try to meet these people in the eyes and too attractive not to do so with this incredible group of performers who were going to go and jump the cliff of this.”

Luca Guadagnino and Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Guadagnino was joined by cast members Andrew Garfield (who plays Altman), Yura Borisov (who plays Sutskever) and Monica Barbaro (who plays Murati) for a post-screening conversation. The actors were challenged with preparing to play real people who they were not able to interact with ahead of time, instead relying on interviews, video recordings, and other research in order to get into their characters.

Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

“[Sam Altman] still is unknowable to me and I'm fascinated by him continuously and exponentially, for here until eternity," Garfield said about OpenAI's co-founder and CEO. “And it's important to try to understand because as Luca said, these are the kids that have the reins of the future and we've somehow allowed them to just hold onto them. And we've kind of given our autonomy over or it's been taken from behind our backs.”

He added: “It's a remarkable thing to have the resilience to go and sleep every night, knowing that you're really doing a lot of damage.”

Barbaro said the fact that Murati is very private helped her understand the former OpenAI CTO. “That is indicative of a kind of behavior and personality type and it pointed me in a certain direction as far as her values were concerned,” she said. “And we also had a lot of wonderful consultants, people who worked with them at OpenAI, but who were no longer with the company, kind of telling us what jokes and things that they would make.”

Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

For Borisov, he hopes his portrayal does Sutskever justice and that people will want to know or understand him more. “I started to watch videos about him and looked at his social media, trying just to understand what he's talking about in his interviews,” the actor explained. "And step by step, as much as I discovered him, it was more and more scary for me because I started to respect and love him more and more."

Monica Barbaro, Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The conversation had its own meta moment of sorts, when Barbaro posed a question to Guiducci about his decision to profile and feature Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair’s New Establishment Issue.

"You faced heat for presenting, maybe some people would say pedestalizing Sam Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair, what is your take on that?" Barbaro asked.

“I think that the magazine is an arena where these things have to play out,” Guiducci said. “It's so interesting to me to...have the [forthcoming] feature about this film in the issue that was preceded by one where I got to ask Sam about it." Guiducci continued: "Something about [taking Sam's] picture makes people feel, ‘Oh, that's the trophy.’ But photojournalism is journalism too. And I want people to be able to look back at the magazine and see a document of the time that we lived in," he said. "And also, if the photo is what helps me get the interview where we get to know more about these people, I'm going to take it.”

Monica Barbaro at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Other panel highlights included the subject of ChatGPT, which only Guadagnino admitted to using occasionally to ask about what’s ok to feed his dogs. He also addressed parting ways with the film's original studio partner Amazon and the fortuitous partnership that emerged with new distributor NEON.

“I think there is some kind of honor in the decision because they could have written off the movie and that's it,” he said about Amazon dropping the film from their slate. “And then they allowed us to find a partner and we found the best partner possible… They really believed in the movie.”

“They really made everything to get us to make the best movie we could,” he continued. "I only have good feelings toward my friends at Amazon. And in a strange way, I kind of understand the decision. Conflict of interest is a big thing.”

Luca Guadagnino at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3623. Barbie Rewind Is Here To Remind Me Of The Pink Childhood I Forgot I Loved

In the waning hours before GTA VI becomes available on my living room console, I am (for now) posted up at my PC, blasting bright, neon pink directly into my retinas. Just like when I was a kid.

Iâve been playing Barbie Rewind in bits and odd pieces. Released last week, itâs another retro game collection from Digital Eclipse that thankfully makes 16 classics playable again for normal people who donât have giant retro console collections, decades after their original releases. One of those gamesâBarbie: Vacation Adventureânever even got a full release until now, and was previously only known via a handful of magazine previews. Now, you can play it.

I like the idea of Barbie Rewind, and Iâm glad these games are available again. But the presentation of this collection leaves a lot wanting. Itâs buggy, for oneâI had weird audio blips in both the Dreamhouse segments (more on those in a moment) and in several of the games, with sound and music cutting out randomly or going fuzzy like a radio. Barbie Super Sports was, I hate to use the phrase but, literally unplayableâonce I got to the skiing section, I couldnât move my character at all in any direction no matter how many times I tried or what buttons I pushed. At one point, I spent so long navigating back and forth in and out of menus trying to check the controls that my menu got stuck on the controls page, leaving me unable to exit the game without hard shutting it down. Unfortunately, doing so erased all of my progress in both Super Sports and two other games I had tried prior, which in turn set me back on my objectives in the Dreamhouse. I also just found most of the games difficult to parse visually in their original resolution on a modern 1080p monitor; surely something should have been done about that?

For that reason, I find the Dreamhouse bit of Barbie Rewind far more compelling than the games that are the actual purpose of the collection. As you play the retro games, you unlock new rooms in a Dreamhouse and new furniture to fill them with. The decor is all taken from Barbie playsets over the years: couches, tables, lamps, phones, beds, and so forth. While the decorating mechanics are pretty simple, the decorations themselves are bright and colorful neons and pastels in funky and often retro shapes and styles, daring you to try to make them fit an orderly theme. Just as I would want a pile of mixed-up playsets to be.

I imagine that those who played with such things growing up will recognize them, but itâs reminded me that despite being a Barbie fiend, I never had any Barbie playsets growing up. Just dolls and clothes. I would build houses for them out of a couple of empty KâNEX boxes, or use the couch and pillows to make small Barbie forts. Iâm a little jealous of whoever got to mess around with all this plastic, though Iâm sure that, had I had any of this, it would have gotten lost like all the little Barbie shoes that disappeared over the years. Itâs not the same, decorating a virtual Dreamhouse. But itâs a nice enough approximation, given that Iâm not about to go out and buy any of this in reality.

Rachel Simone Weil, a girls video game and toy historian, played a major role in getting the Dreamhouse aspects together. She served as a historical consultant on Barbie Rewind, and especially focused on making sure the Dreamhouse elements were an accurate and celebratory portrayal of Barbie history. Obviously, Barbie Rewind could not include every single playset ever made, so Weil had to be selective as she tapped into different aspects of Barbie history. What were the most important relics of Barbie history?

âObviously, the iconic playsets, the ones that fans remember, those really tactile memories of just the feeling of the plastic or the way the box smelled,â she said. âThere are certain playsets, I think, that are really emblematic of the brand. I think of the Beach Blast pool. That’s pretty iconic. Obviously, the original Barbie Dreamhouse. We also included some deep cuts. There’s Cafe Today, which is pretty rare and hard to come by, especially in good condition, but a beautiful, psychedelic-designed cafe.â

In addition to the mix of iconic sets and deep cuts, Weil also wanted to emphasize technology, given the video game-ness of Barbie Rewind. And Barbie has quite the technological history. Weil tells me about playsets from before I was born making a point to include computers, phones, record players, CD players, and so forth. Barbie was always hip, always on top of the latest trends both in fashion and in tech.

âThe Barbie Dreamhouse from 1979 has this nightstand with this little tiny computer in it,â Weil says. Iâve seen it, I have it in my Barbie Rewind Dreamhouse currently, and it looks wonderfully retro and ridiculous. âAnd in â79, personal computers were just starting to come out. So, you’re starting to see people imagining what computers might be, right? And then you see Day to Night Barbie in the â80s, you start to see the IBM PC style playset computers.

âOh, another one I really like is the travel agent playset from, I think, 1986. The travel industry was famously one of the first industries to adopt computer technology. And right as it’s happening, Barbie is there with that travel agent playset and she’s got a computer. And the home office playsets from the â80s and â90s. Barbie’s got a home computer. She goes to work and she does computers.â

Barbie was a massive, massive part of my childhood. For a solid eight, nine, ten years, Barbie was one of my predominant interests. Dressing up those dolls, taking them to friendsâ houses, and playing make-believe was formative for me, and two of the video games in this collection (Barbie Super Sports and Barbie Race and Ride) represent my earliest memories of playing video games at all. I was playing Barbie long before I had my hands on Mario or Zelda.

And yet, Barbie is rarely if ever considered to be on equal footing with those classics. In some ways, I get itâmainstream gaming is bent far more toward the kinds of games that Mario and Zelda evolved to become. And yet, Infinity Nikki is massive. So is The Sims. The Style Savvy series on Nintendo handhelds was super popular, as were animal-focused games like Nintendogs. Heck, we just heard everyone praising Dressmaker. These games have always been with us, and Barbie pioneered a lot of what they would become. Itâs unfortunately not too hard to work out why Barbie doesnât get the respect she deserves.

âBarbie Rewind is the first retro game compilation that centers predominantly girl-led experiences in console gaming, right, of the 20th century,â Weil says. âThese games were a big deal when they came out in terms of popularity, sales, and it’s not just about the market impact. These games had a big, like, left a big impression on the people that played them, right?

âGirls who played these games in the â80s, â90s, â00s are adults now, and they’re looking back on these games with fondness and nostalgia and stories about, you know, negotiating with their siblings about who got the controller and the hours poured into them. There’s really not beenâI’d say there’s been a lack of an outlet for that fondness or way to revisit these games or even an acknowledgement from the world that these Barbie games, they weren’t just a fever dream, not only were they real, but we can play them again on modern platforms. So, I think for Digital Eclipse and Atari to put out this collection in collaboration with Mattel, I think it’s really gratifying, a gratifying acknowledgement that women’s retro gaming experiences are valid, important, and they’re part of the broader retro gaming culture at large, and they deserve to be included.â

Itâs not just girls, either. David Lowey, director of marketing at Atari, is here to champion girl games for everyone. âIt’s amazing how many people I’ve spoken to, particularly guys I’ve spoken to, who have played a significant amount of these games. And the answer is always the same. It was like, âYeah, it was on the PC in the kitchen. It was my sister’s game, but I played the hell out of it.â I heard that so much.â

Recently, an interview with the developers of Dressmaker sparked some social media discussion around women as gamers, and whether they are being adequately served by games that reflect their interests. Itâs a tricky discussion. On one hand, itâs obviously narrow-minded to assume that women are only going to be interested in games about fashion and vacation and pet rescue and horses. But on the other, it is true that many women do find those things interesting, and that because those things are typically associated with women, games like the ones in Barbie Rewind are less common and often not as well-funded or supported as more âmasculineâ games.

Weil had not seen the Dressmaker discourse when I spoke to her and thus didnât want to comment on the interview specifically, but I asked her to tell me more broadly: what are we talking about when we talk about Girl Games? What does it mean for a game to be a Girl Game?

âFirst of all, it’s changed a lot in the last 15 years,â she says. âI think 15 years ago it was very difficult to have that conversation. I remember being in grad school and having professors say, âyou can’t study Barbie video games.â I remember having an exhibit vandalized. People were upset about the idea that we would talk about girlsâ video games, or that acknowledging that they existed and celebrating those memories was the same as saying, âgirls must do this, and girls must love pink and whatever.â And so it’s a difficult conversation.â

Weil goes on to say that she intentionally uses the phrase âgirl gameâ to provoke that difficult conversation: to get people talking about the dichotomy between what girls must be, what they can be, and what theyâre allowed to be.

âOne thing that I think about as a historian is that this scrutiny of girl games, [where people ask], âIs this set modeling the right behaviors for girls? Is this setting up the right expectations for what femininity means and all this stuff?â We’re not asking those same questions about boy games. We’re not asking, is Mega Man a good role model for boys? Is Mega Man going to teach boys to, you know, be this or that? Or, if we’re asking those questions, it’s not preventing Mega Man from being part of retro gaming canon, right?

âFor me as a historian, I’m not saying we shouldn’t ask those questions, or we shouldn’t talk about those social issues. But I think we have a tendency to let the pendulum swing too far and say, âthere are social issues around this. And so let’s put all the Barbie games in the trash.â We can’t do that. I think the history of girlsâ video games has been forgotten and rediscovered like three or four times because this behavior of saying, âThis is a delicate subject, this touches on social topics or discrimination or stereotypes or things like that. And I feel nervous about that. And so I’m just going to pretend that these games didn’t exist.â We can’t do that.â

Did FBI plant the seeds for another spinoff?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Warning! Spoilers ahead for FBI Season 9, Episode 7, “Posterity,” streaming now with a Paramount+ subscription.

With FBI now in its ninth season on the 2026 TV schedule, the stakes have certainly been rising, and I’m not just talking about the professional ones. A show like FBI not only digs into the work aspect of the characters but the personal lives as well, even if it’s not shown as much. This week’s episode had a particularly surprising personal update for one of the characters, and that made me realize I had to ask the stars about spinoff potential.

Shantel VanSanten returned to FBI as Special Agent Nina Chase in Monday’s episode, “Posterity,” which marked her second appearance on the series since FBI: Most Wanted’s cancellation in 2025. Her return came just a couple of weeks after it was revealed that Nina had been offered a job to lead her own task force in San Diego, leading Scola (John Boyd) to question the logistics of their relationship and raising their son, Dougie. As Nina continued to pack and get in one last case at 26 Fed, Scola was still wrestling with how they were going to make things work. Ultimately, he told Nina he was going to put in a transfer and follow her to San Diego, meaning another FBI exit could be looming.

As Scola pointed out, though, it will still probably be a while until the transfer goes through. However, with him eventually moving out to California and Scolina taking the FBI by storm down there, this has spinoff potential written all over it. It would be fun to follow Scola and Nina in San Diego as Nina led her own task force, but would it ever happen? VanSanten and Boyd gave their take to CinemaBlend and, hilariously, have their own opinions on the ordeal:

FBI has been growing as a franchise, like any Dick Wolf series, so it’s totally logical to wonder about a spinoff coming from this update. Having two fan-favorite characters moving across the country for the job would certainly be a missed opportunity for another series, in my humble opinion. While it sounds like there aren’t any plans, and Boyd seems to be sticking around on FBI for the time being, if VanSanten has her way, we very well could be getting a Scolina spinoff at some point in the future. While we wait and hope for that, I'm just glad that it seems like Nina is finally getting closure.

As for what could happen in a potential Scolina spinoff, well, the possibilities are endless. Nina leading her own task force and seeing how she evolves in that leadership position would definitely be a great focus point. Scola would probably be settling into a new FBI field office, but the two of them would still stick to their deal of not going on cases together. We’d also probably get more of them and Dougie, who we definitely have not seen enough of. The story is there, and so are the characters, and I would love it if it happened. But if not, I’d hope that Boyd isn’t leaving FBI any time soon.

Now, for the time being, Scola will continue working out of 26 Fed. Considering all the cast changes that FBI has been through in recent years, I’m hoping that Boyd doesn’t leave the series any time soon, no matter how much I want a Scolina spinoff. Nina may be moving, but fans can still see Scola and co. in new episodes of FBI on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming the next day on Paramount+.

#3620. Lindsay Clancy Makes Another Bid to Drop Murder Charges Before Retrial

Lindsay Clancy’s defense team has called on Massachusetts’ highest court to intervene ahead of her upcoming retrial in her latest bid to have her murder charges dropped.

In a petition filed Monday, November 16, with the state’s Supreme Judicial Court, Clancy’s lawyers asked to reverse Plymouth County Superior Court Judge William Sullivan’s recent denial of Clancy’s motion to dismiss the charges, per Boston.com. Sullivan’s decision cleared the way for a retrial.

The day of the petition’s filing, Sullivan scheduled Clancy’s second murder trial to take place on March 29, 2027.

Clancy, of Duxbury, sought to have the charges she’s facing in the killings of her three children dismissed on double jeopardy grounds after Sullivan declared a mistrial in her case on September 4.

Clancy’s attorneys argue in their petition that she was “aggrieved” by Sullivan turning down her motion to dismiss on November 9.

“Respectfully, contrary to the trial court’s stated belief at the time, it did have viable choices other than declaring a mistrial,” her attorneys wrote in the filing.

They contend she “should not be ‘forced to run the gantlet’ again” after a deadlocked 11-1 jury couldn’t unanimously agree on whether she was criminally liable for the January 2023 deaths of her children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

Clancy’s defense team argues Sullivan should’ve investigated the lone holdout juror further after the jury foreperson alleged the man, Michael P. Desronvil, didn’t follow instructions relating to reasonable doubt.

“There is a substantial possibility that the trial court, after inquiry, would have discharged the non-compliant juror,” her attorneys wrote in the petition. “Such possibility, therefore, constitutes a viable alternative to the mistrial, precluding a finding of manifest necessity.”

One justice is reviewing the petition, which requests for oral arguments to be held and for a referral to the entire court, Boston.com reported.

Clancy hasn’t denied killing her children. Her defense team, however, has maintained she shouldn’t be held criminally responsible because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis ahead of their deaths. Prosecutors have alleged she intended to kill her children.

After prosecutors shared on Monday that they planned to retry Clancy, Clancy’s attorney Kevin Reddington told the Daily Mail that his client “knows that at least this case has been and will be able to put a light on the treatment of women with mental health issues.”

Reddington also addressed the possibility of Clancy taking the stand during her retrial.

“That’s one of those issues that you have to wait to find out,” he told the news outlet.

The James Bond role may have come (indirectly) due to Zendaya introducing Pattinson to director Denis Villeneuve, who is not only at the helm of Dune, but upcoming, as-yet-untitled James Bond 26 as well. #3618. Tallulah Willis: I Stayed Out Past My Bedtime to Celebrate My Mom at the Baby2Baby Gala

The whole endeavor began as it usually does, with a search for the perfect dress. Turns out it would be a yellow Carolina Herrera column-shaped confection (if you care), teetering on yellow satin pointed peekaboo-toe platforms, with my first press pass thudding around in my corresponding yellow duchess satin clutch.

Stylist Brad Goreski and his assistant Clarke, who work with my mother, Demi Moore, sourced the ensemble after finding Mom’s beautiful black ruffled two-piece (adorably also Carolina Herrera).

Around 6:50 p.m. on Saturday, my older sisters, Scout (in cocoa-brown beaded Elie Saab) and Rumer (in whimsical archival Vera Wang), florist Eric Buterbaugh, Brad, my mom and I are about to leave her house for the Baby2Baby Gala, an annual fundraiser for the non-profit that dedicated to providing diapers, clothing, and other basic necessities to children and families in need across the country.

Demi is taking photos against a pale brown backdrop when I hear her say, marginally worried, “Yes, the outfit is amazing, but they didn’t give me pockets.” I cannot fault her. A pocket, particularly in an evening gown, creates an entirely different architecture for one’s night.

When we make it to the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, Rihanna is blasting and a gorgeous electric General Motors car, part of the silent auction, is parked out front. I’m holding the bottom of my dress to avoid any “yard sales” on the carpeted floor when I hear, “Is it you? I hope it’s you!” It’s my very new, lovely friend Jackie Tohn, whom I met at a Nobody Wants This premiere party.

Inside, beautifully dressed people laugh and chat. I spot Miranda Kerr, who is both a Baby2Baby board member and major donor, and pass Nara Smith leaning over a dolled-up Elsa Hosk while “Espresso” blasts from overhead speakers.

Table 4 is front and center. Some could say the best seats in the house. Fitting, as Baby2Baby is honoring my mother with the Giving Tree Award tonight. The scene around our table is a frenzy of joyful energy. I make a beeline for Paris Hilton to thank her for the facial I received at her spa this week, while Dancing With the Stars alums Rumer and Jenna Dewan immediately pull out their phones to compare pictures of their kids.

Then I spot Sofia Richie Grainge and her husband, Atlantic Records CEO Elliot Grainge. I snake through throngs of elegant people and poke Elliot’s back twice. “Elliot, it’s Tallulah! We went to Wildwood together!” He instantly remembers me. “Tallulah was the cool girl in class,” he tells Sofia. I blush, but don’t feel the need to correct him.

Scout approaches and says, almost incredulously, “Hi, I’m Scout…you guys just signed me at Atlantic Records.” Elliot grabs her shoulders. “We’re so happy to have you. Are you happy with us?” She can’t say “yes” fast enough.

The program begins with Keke Palmer, who completely owns the stage, telling hilarious stories about her son before shifting into heartfelt candor about the gift of watching him grow. Kerry Washington thanks the sponsors and announces Baby2Baby’s new permanent headquarters, “a promise to millions of children. Not just for today, but for decades to come.”

Then Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein, the organization’s CEOs, come to the stage, sharing the work—no, the magic—they have created over 15 years. Their first gala in 2012 raised $1 million. Last year’s raised $18 million. To date, they’ve distributed an astonishing 850 million essential items to people in need across all 50 states, responded to over 150 disasters, developed their own diaper production line during COVID, and expanded into mental health support for new mothers. The mission remains the same, but the scale is impossible to comprehend.

Now Rumer, Scout, and I are all crying during a short video about two families impacted by Baby2Baby. The feeling is palpable for the rest of the room.

As the live auction begins, I catch my mom discreetly reading over a printout of her speech. I don’t feel nerves coming off her, but a desire to match the elegance and integrity surrounding us.

Andrew Garfield takes the stage and speaks directly to my mom about the woman he knows. “She is a miracle,” he says.

Then it’s Demi’s turn. Holding her gleaming award in two hands, she thanks Andrew for carving out time amid his Artificial press tour. My mother adores Andrew, a feeling shared across our family.

Alone on stage in her Carolina gown (sans pockets), she asks everyone to breathe. “Inhale. Exhale.” That breath, she says, is the relief Baby2Baby provides when a mother no longer has to choose between dinner and diapers. “Your child matters, you matter, and you are not alone.” She leaves us with the idea that the essence of this work is to be remarkably human. Baby to baby, mother to mother, soul to soul.

Then Cardi B takes the stage and the atmosphere shifts with a jolt. Everyone is on their feet dancing. The official after-party begins, but I’m turning back into a pumpkin in towering satin stilettos. It was a remarkably beautiful night, and I’m left with the overwhelming desire to do more—to show up for someone who may not have the ability to show up for themselves or their precious loved ones.

But for this on-scene reporter’s inaugural correspondence, it was ultimately Baby2Baby2Bedtime.

#3617. This Fighting Game Is Nominated For A TGA Despite Development Shutting Down

Earlier today, Geoff Keighley announced all of the nominees for The Game Awards 2026, the annual celebration of gaming held in Los Angeles. Among expected nominees Grand Theft Auto VI, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and Control Resonant was one surprising name: 2XKO has been nominated for Best Fighting Game, despite Riot Games announcing the end of the game's lifecycle earlier this year.

Riot announced that "active development" for the fighting game, featuring characters from League of Legends, would end in December 2026. "Over the last few months, we’ve been monitoring 2XKO’s trajectory closely, and what we’ve seen is painting a clear, consistent picture," Riot said at the time. "While a lot of you jumped in to try the game and there’s an incredible community that plays every day, we haven’t seen enough players stick with the game to get to a path toward sustainability,”

Riot's fighter is joined in the Best Fighting Game category by Invincible Vs., Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, Avatar Legends, and My Hero Academia: All's Justice. 2XKO is also not the only game on this list whose future is in jeopardy; soon after it launched in April, Invincible Vs. developer Quarter up laid off reportedly 75% of its staff, while saying that future updates were dependent on the game's overall sales.

UPDATE 11/18/2026: Skybound has commented on upcoming plans for Invincible Vs. with the following statement:

"We understand there have been some questions surrounding the future of Invincible VS, but we want to reassure players that we're continuing to support the game and have more content planned. Most recently, we launched Season 2 introducing Angstrom Levy as the game's third DLC fighter, expanding the roster to 21 playable characters, alongside the all-new Challenges Mode, giving players new ways to test their skills and earn rewards. Season 3 arrives in December, bringing additional content, challenges and the newest playable fighter, Agent Spider.

Looking ahead, we have more content planned for 2027, with additional details to be shared soon. We're excited about what's ahead for Invincible VS and look forward to continuing to support the game and its community."

Grand Theft Auto VI received the most nominations for a single game at this year's ceremony with eight, including Game of the Year. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem tied for the second-most nominations with six each, while Phantom Blade Zero rounded out the top three with five nominations. Nintendo earned the most nominations for a single publisher, meanwhile, with 12 across the event's 30 awards.

The Game Awards is set to take place December 10 live from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, California.

#3616. BioWare Is Dead, But Mass Effect’s Spiritual Successor Exodus Just Gave Us A Glimpse of A Spicy Romance

For the first time since its announcement during December 2023's The Game Awards, players are getting a look at the female player-character from its upcoming sci-fi RPG Exodus--which was full of Mass Effect DNA back when we previewed it in September.

The default female version of main character Jun Aslan was revealed today via a seven-minute featurette showing off both female-Jun's face and a bit more of the game itself. The trailer also provided a glimpse of a brief romance scene between female-Jun and Suliman, who is one of the game's romanceable NPCs.

When GameSpot previewed the game, only male-Jun was playable, and we didn't get a chance to romance Suliman, but we did manage to earn his approval, suggesting he may be into both masculine and feminine Jun. We also didn't see the character creator, but there certainly appears to be one, as we see Jun sporting a different look during the romantic encounter with Suliman, with voice actress Carina Corti (Mafia: The Old Country, Little Death) providing Jun's voice throughout both scenes.

Jun's male character model recently got a complete makeover after players complained his original look wasn't pleasing to the eye, but up until today, it wasn't clear who was voicing him. Today, Archetype shared that Stephen Oyoung (Marvel's Spider-Man, Marvel's Spider-Man 2) will be voicing the character.

The female-Jun reveal is followed by a featurette called Scrappy Salvager, featuring a behind-the-scenes look at Jun's origins and the way players' decision can impact Jun's trajectory early on in the game.

"We think of players as the co-authors of our story, and that applies to Jun as well," game director Chris King explains in the video. 

Art director Mark Anderson describes Jun as a "little fish in a really big pond," rather than starting off as a typical hero ready to save the world. Additionally, the featurette goes into more detail about Jun's "precognition" ability, which allows them to see glimpses of possible futures. If interpreted correctly, these premonitions may help players make choices that benefit them. But misunderstanding them may lead to consequences that expand far beyond Jun and their friends. Due to the way the game's time dilation mechanic works, player choices can have unexpected effects that impact civilizations for centuries.

After the death of BioWare, it seems the Mass Effect formula will live on in Exodus, with its vast worlds, strange alien races, NPC romances, and narrative choices. It shouldn't come as a surprise, of course--Exodus developer Archetype Entertainment was founded in 2019 by BioWare veterans James Ohlen, Drew Karpshyn, and Chad Robertson.

Exodus launches on April 7, 2027 and is available to wishlist now on the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, Steam, and the Epic Games Store.

#3613. Penélope Cruz Says She and Husband Javier Bardem are “Very Careful” About Choosing When to Work Together

Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem are very selective about when they work on a project together, but the opportunity to costar in director Florian Zeller's timely psychological thriller Bunker was too enticing to pass up.

"When [Zeller] came to us with this powerful, very necessary story to tell, we looked at each other and there was no way to say no to this," Cruz said during a post-screening discussion at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room on Sunday. "I'm very, very happy that we did it."

Bunker revolves around a married couple, Miguel (Bardem) and Sofia (Cruz), whose 17-year marriage is tested when Miguel, a famous architect, is presented with a life changing work opportunity.

“I really wanted to work with them because I truly believe they are [two] of the greatest actors working today,” Zeller said during the panel discussion moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross. “I was also very excited and interested to have them together onscreen because they are also a real couple. I thought it would be an interesting and unique opportunity to approach something that has to do with authenticity, with the truth. Not to say that this is their story, because of course this is not their story.”

Florian Zeller at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

Cruz said she felt a kinship with her character's concerns. “We have so many things in common in terms of this sadness and frustration and anger that you feel in terms of where is the world going if we don't wake up soon,” she said. “I hope it's not too late, but especially the experiment that is being done on younger people, children, teenagers, it just makes me very furious.

“It's something that affects me so much as an actress, as a mother, as a citizen of the world, that I felt completely a need to play Sophia,” she continued. “And of course it was not the only reason, but it was a big privilege to be able to say those lines. And [Zeller] is such a master of writing and I am a fan of all his work. And same for Javier, who is not here with us today, he's doing theater, but we are very careful in terms of choosing when to work together.”

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

Cruz praised Zeller’s ability to provide a supportive, safe working environment and his strong point of view. “We felt really, really safe with him, he's so talented. He doesn't need any kind of manipulation and he never treats the audience as not intelligent because the audience can feel everything,” she explained. “And that has become really the most important thing for me. Don't over-explain, don't underestimate the audience ever because the thermometer is really working. And also with young people more and more and more. That is my hope to continue to go to see films on a big screen. They're coming back thank God. So let's create more possibilities so they can keep doing that.”

Cruz also said that she and Bardem have similar approaches to their work and the preparation it requires. “It's true that we share the same passion and we have done this since we were teenagers,” she said. “We love exploring and studying and feeling that healthy fear of the unknown because every time you begin a project, in a way, it's really starting from zero. So it's a really good thing to share.”

Zeller called his collaboration with the couple “a fascinating journey. It takes a lot of courage or fearlessness to do that, I think, for actors.” He also revealed that he initially referenced Stanley Kubrick's seminal thriller Eyes Wide Shut as a point of reference for Bunker, but realized it might not be setting the proper tone, given the circumstances.

“I remember that the first time I spoke with [Cruz] and Javier about this project, I mentioned a film that was somewhere in my mind, Eyes Wide Shut. Not to say that there is any kind of connection between the two films, but as you remember, Eyes Wide Shut at the time, Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman, they were together," he said. "And I remember as a viewer that it was so interesting to be in a position where you do not know exactly what you're invited to watch… but Javier [later] told me, ‘You should not mention this film too often because remember at the end of the shooting they broke up.’ And then I realized that the director, Kubrick, died soon after. So I was like, ‘Okay, I'm going to stop mentioning this film.’ But the real difference I would say is that we knew that the destination of that film was the last image of the painting that you saw, which means that it was about how to reconnect with the other.”

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

Landman is making quite the splash down in Texas right now, as people saw the show being filmed at a Texas Christian University game over the weekend. Then, not long after that, Ali Larter posted a photo dump from filming, and it featured one person I never expected to see: Glen Powell.

Of course, I’m well aware that Glen Powell is dating Michelle Randolph, Larter’s on-screen daughter and a veteran of Taylor Sheridan’s shows. He’s also famously from and lives in Texas, which is where Landman is filmed. So, it’s not illogical for him to be around the set of this popular Paramount+ show. However, I was still surprised to see him in the final slide of Larter’s photo dump. Take a look:

In that final slide, you can see Larter posing for a photo with her co-stars, Billy Bob Thornton and Michelle Randolph, as well as Glen Powell.

Now, Landman has actually been filming at Texas Christian University since October, per the university. However, it made headlines over the weekend because Randolph was spotted with the cheerleaders on Saturday during the game against the Kansas State Wildcats.

In Landman, she plays Ainsley Norris, the daughter of Thornton’s Tommy and Larter’s Angela. She’s a student at TCU, and a big part of her storyline has to do with her joining the cheer team. It would seem it will be an even bigger part of her arc in Season 3, seeing as not only was Randolph seen filming at this game, but Larter and Bobbi Salvör Menuez, who play Paigyn, were there too.

To top it all off, Glen Powell was also spotted at the game. As you can see in the third image of this carousel TCU uploaded, the Twisters actor was on the sidelines – which is also where his girlfriend happened to be.

A post shared by TCU (@texaschristianuniversity)

Rumors that Powell and Randolph were dating picked up in late 2025, and the actors went Instagram official in July of this year. Since then, they’ve posted pictures of each other here and there, and the Running Man star’s dog, Brisket, even made a cameo in one of the 1923 actress’s photo dumps.

Speaking of Brisket, Powell’s dog also gives him another tie to Landman. In early 2025, Brisket met up with Demi Moore’s pup, Pilaf. Man, it’s really a small world, and maybe I shouldn’t be shocked that he now has a connection to another star of this Taylor Sheridan show.

Overall, it was very cute to see the Top Gun: Maverick star pop up in a photo dump all about Landman. Clearly, he’s being a supportive partner and cheering Randolph on as she literally cheers on TCU. I also bet it’s pretty cool to just say you get to hang out with her, Ali Larter, Billy Bob Thornton, and Sam Elliott.

Now, I think the question becomes: Could we get Glen Powell on Landman? Taylor Sheridan has a tendency to hire A-listers for his shows, so I don’t think it’s out of the question. Plus, these images make it clear that the Chad Powers star is already literally very close to the production.

#3611. WoW: Forever Weekly Player Numbers Are The Highest For Blizzard’s MMO In 15 Years

World of Warcraft: Forever continues to break ground for developer Blizzard, which revealed new stats related to Forever's already record-breaking launch.

Forever launched on November 4, and it didn't take long for Blizzard to announce that the game, the third major version of Blizzard's MMORPG, was the biggest launch in WoW history in terms of concurrent and returning players.

Now, Blizzard is revealing more launch stats. Holly Longdale, executive producer and vice president for WoW, announced on social media that Forever has "more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years."

The tidbit translates to Forever having more weekly active players than any WoW release since the game's 2010 Cataclysm expansion. That's quite the accomplishment considering that time period also includes massively popular expansions like 2016's Legion and the release of WoW Classic in 2019.

That wasn't the only statistic Blizzard had to share. It revealed that more than 15 million characters have been created in Forever, with nearly 1.5 billion quests completed so far. It also shared the game's deadliest boss, Archmage Arugal from the Shadowfang Keep dungeon, as well as nearly 29 million PvP kills and almost 197 million player deaths. You can check out the full statistics below.

While fun, Blizzard's stats don't reveal the numbers that more than a few players are likely curious about, like Forever's most popular races and classes. For that, players have to rely on third-party fan sites that have tracked Forever statistics since launch.

Forever's launch may be breaking records, but that wasn't enough to score the MMO a nod at The Game Awards 2026. In other WoW Forever news, Blizzard recently made yet another big change to dungeons.

#3610. Alec and Hilaria Baldwin Joke 'Gaslighting' Is the Secret to Their Marriage

Alec Baldwin and wife Hilaria Baldwin revealed that a good sense of humor — and “a lot of gaslighting” — is the secret to their nearly 15-year marriage.

“I think it’s our banter,” Hilaria, 42, exclusively told Us of the pair’s relationship on Tuesday, November 17, while attending Tony Bennett’s 100th Birthday Benefit in New York City. “It keeps us both getting old very fast and young, both the things at the same time.”

Alec, 68, revealed that some slight decorating changes, courtesy of his wife, keeps him on his toes, too.

“I come home and the house is completely redecorated,” he told Us, which Hilaria confirmed as true.

“Yes, every day when he leaves, if I don’t have to work, I come home [and decorate],” she admitted.

Alec, who married Hilaria in 2012, joked, “I come home and I’m like, ‘Whose idea was this?’ And she says, ‘Don’t worry about it.’”

Hilaria confessed, “I tell him it was his idea, and he’s like, ‘Wait a minute.”

Alec confirmed his wife’s shenanigans, saying she’ll ask him, “Don’t you remember, this was your idea? We talked about this.”

Hilaria, who shares seven children with her husband, teased, “See we can both gaslight each other.” (Alec is also the father of daughter Ireland Baldwin, whom he shares with ex-wife Kim Basinger.)

Alec, while grinning, added, “A lot of gaslighting. The key to a happy marriage is a lot of gaslighting.”

“Yes, gaslighting, but banter,” Hilaria chimed in when talking about their success as a couple. “And then we’re both not sure what’s real and not real anymore, but we both do it to each other.”

The keys to Alec and Hilaria’s marriage aren’t the only things that the pair see eye to eye on.

The Baldwins are both big fans of the late Tony Bennett, who died in 2023 at the age of 96, and his legacy, telling Us that they came out to support Tony Bennett’s 100th Birthday Benefit in honor of their personal connection to the Grammy winner.

“We have known Tony and his family for years, and supporting the foundation, exploring the arts, the school they built, all those things, that was a big thing for us,” Alec told Us on the red carpet. “Because I had a very surprising and unexpected friendship with Tony, and he was great. I loved him.”

The comedian recalled working with Bennett on Saturday Night Live when the famed musician played a Tony Bennett impersonator for a sketch.

“That was the pinnacle of my career,” Alec shared. “Literally, that was a high point.”

He added that he and Hilaria know Tony’s son Danny Bennett and “his whole family” and they’ve been “working whenever we can to come to these events and support Tony.”

Hilaria noted that she “always” thinks of Tony as “the beginning” of her relationship with Alec, because the singer was “such an important figure” to them.

“I realized how big of a heart Tony [had], but Alec as well of how much giving and the two of them together,” she recalled. “One of the things I really loved about Tony and I think about regularly is gratitude. He’s like one of the most grateful people in the world. He just loves being in. He’s a good guy.”

During the event, Tony’s legacy of love and gratitude was given an even bigger platform when Exploring the Arts (ETA) and Third Street Music School announced their plan to open the Tony Bennett Institute for Arts Education at Third Street (TBIAE), describing it as a “new initiative bringing together two established organizations to expand access to high-quality arts education and create more opportunities for young people to discover and develop their creative potential,” according to a press release.

TBIAE represents “a new chapter in Tony’s legacy during the year he would have celebrated his 100th birthday, which also coincides with the 25th anniversary of Frank Sinatra School of the Arts, the public high school [Tony] and his wife, Susan Benedetto, founded in his hometown of Astoria, Queens,” per the foundation’s statement.

Alec, for his part, joined Danny, 72, on stage during the event to help unveil the plans for the institute.

“These kids are focused, joyful, and proud. You can feel that someone believed in them. That was thanks to Tony and Susan,” he said of Tony and Susan’s commitment to arts education. “Tony used to say he wanted to leave the world a little more beautiful than he found it. Mission accomplished.”

For more details on the Tony Bennett Institute for Arts Education visit www.exploringthearts.org.
