Yellowjackets is arguably one of the best Paramount+ shows, although it required fans to get a Paramount+ subscription including Showtime. I'm personally a hardcore fan who is hyped about the fourth and final season's premiere this month. Folks are hoping to have Yellowjackets' biggest mysteries solved before it ends its run, and hopefully joins the ranks of TV shows that actually ended well. We know that the series guards it secrets from the public, but it turns out that even the cast is left in the dark about spoilers.

Yellowjackets' cast is an incredible multi-generational ensemble who tell the story across two timelines. The pressure is on for the Emmy-nominated series to stick the landing, and provide answers about various long-standing mysteries. In a recent interview with ScreenRant, Teen Shauna actress Sophie Nélisse was asked if she knew her character's fate ahead of time, to which she said:

No, we actually don't get the scripts more than like a week in advance, which is kind of fun because on set we're all sort of plotting and trying to reflect on what we have. We were coming up with our own theories of what the finale was going to look like, but we had no idea how they were going to get rescued, how their time in the wilderness would end. I obviously knew that Shauna was going to get married because we saw that.

Well, my mind is blown. While Yellowjackets fans are being kept away from spoilers, I had no idea how tight the security was for even the cast. They only got each new script a week in advance, so Nélisse and her costars weren't able to use the full arc of their character to inform each performance. Instead they had to take things episode by episode and play each moment with honesty without looking ahead.

Fans have lingering questions about the No Eyed Man as well as the mystery involving Crystal's dead body. While we're still in the dark for now, so was the cast. The Heated Rivalry actress went on to say:

We just kind of went day by day with it. We were just always so excited when we got a new script because, as the audience feels when they finish an episode, it always kind of leaves us on a cliffhanger. That's how, whenever we read a script, we'd all message in the group chat, being like, ‘Oh, this one is so good! I love this bit, and I love that bit.’

Celebrities: sometimes they really are just like us. Despite being the actors bringing Yellowjackets to life, they were left with episode cliffhangers in the midst of shooting Season 4. I have to wonder if Sophie Nélisse and her co-stars even know all the twists that are coming with the show's final season on the air.

Yellowjackets Season 4 will premiere on November 20th as part of the 2026 TV schedule. The pressure is on for the drama series to stick the landing, but it looks like we'll get plenty of surprises in the final set of episodes.

#3583. GTA 6 Is Apparently Everything Rockstar Promised And Then Some

At long last, Grand Theft Auto 6 launch day has come. With Rockstar's latest project steadily unlocking as the clock strikes midnight worldwide, GTA 6 reviews have gone live, and the praise has been overwhelmingly positive so far. In fact, GTA 6 is reviewing so well that it's currently tied with the 1998 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated game of all time on GameSpot's sister site Metacritic, a feat that has taken 28 years to equal.

So what are the reviewers saying? Amongst the flurry of perfect scores, a lot of the consensus is geared toward the world that Rockstar Games has created for its co-protagonists to inhabit, a sandbox that reacts to you in a variety of unique and interesting ways. It's a genre-defining experience for open-world games, as Rockstar has raised the bar to a tremendously high level for any other open-world game that'll follow in its footsteps.

Here's what some reviewers have to say, and for more on the game, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub for an evolving collection of walkthroughs, tips, and tricks.

Grand Theft Auto 6

  • Platforms: PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
  • Price $80 for the Standard Edition, $100 for the Ultimate Edition
  • Release date: November 19

GameSpot -- 10/10

Only Rockstar commands the time and money necessary to make a game as dedicated to small details. And only Rockstar can execute on the realizing such a granular vision unimpeachably. The obsession with the minutia both explains and justifies the 13-year wait. This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.  -- Tamoor Hussain [Full review]

IGN -- 100

Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played. -- Luke Reilly [Full review]

The Guardian -- 5/5

With realism that defies belief, this vast game easily accommodates its trademark foulmouthed, over the top chaos--as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its center -- Keza MacDonald [Full review]

Destructoid -- 10/10

Grand Theft Auto 6 is part criminal come-up tale, part love story, and part life sim all wrapped up in an impossibly deep and detailed Rockstar Games open world that may never run out of things to do. For the last three-plus weeks, I have been gleefully vacationing in Vice City: robbing banks, fighting drug dealers, stealing cars, and enjoying the view while not coming close to finishing everything it has to offer. GTA 6 is finally here now, and it was well worth the wait. -- Scott Duwe [Full review]

Eurogamer -- 5/5

A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that. -- Chris Tapsell [Full review]

Bloomberg -- 5/5

It turns out that the secret ingredients to a great game are a lot of money, time and talented people. -- Jason Schreier [Full review]

Game Informer -- 10/10

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love. -- Matt Miller [Full review]

SiliconEra -- 90/100

Rockstar made strides in incorporating all the systems and the open world into the campaign in a satisfying way. But Jason and Lucia are the glue that keeps everything together. It’s their chemistry and complicity that made me want to experience everything, and it’s them that will keep me coming back. -- Daniel Bueno [Full review]

Screenhub -- 4/5

At its core, GTA 6 is a pretty good game. There are large sections where it is an absolutely epic game, and large sections that are boring and too limited. However, after I pushed through the boring parts and it opened up enough to become a proper GTA title, it became worth it. Regardless of whether the game was good, it was always going to be an inescapable cultural moment. Luckily, it’s one largely worth participating in. -- Alice Clarke [Full review]

Kotaku -- No score

GTA 6 is a truly remarkable game. A masterpiece of open-world design that brings forward the best parts of all of Rockstar’s past games into one billion-dollar adventure that is unlike anything I’ve played before. It’s a game I’ll be playing for years, and I can’t wait to talk about it with others. -- Zack Zwiezen [Full review]

The Verge -- No score

It really seemed like no project could live up to the level of scrutiny that GTA VI has been and will be subjected to. But now we can forget all of that, because GTA 6is actually here. And the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it. -- Andrew Webster [Full review]

#3582. Zendaya “Felt Overwhelmed” on the Set of ‘The Odyssey.’ Luckily, Tom Holland Came to Support Her

On the set of The Odyssey, in which Zendaya plays the goddess Athena, there were some particularly challenging days, as the actor recalled during a recent special screening attended by the cast at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. While filming certain scenes—especially those with a crowd of extras—the 30-year-old actor felt “incredibly nervous,” she said.

How did she manage to keep the situation under control? Thank her husband, Tom Holland, whom Zendaya says went to set that day to cheer her up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day star Holland also appears in The Odyssey as Telemachus, son of Odysseus and Penelope. And although he wasn’t scheduled to work at that particular moment, he showed up anyway to support his wife.

Matt Damon’s Odysseus consults with Zendaya’s Athena in The Odyssey.

“I felt overwhelmed, to say the least,” Zendaya said at the screening, as reported by the Daily Mail, with the actor looking stunning in her cream-colored one-shoulder dress, pixie cut, and Christian Louboutin stilettos. “It was interesting because I was on a night shoot, and I remember I came in and I was like, This is like, a pinch-me moment…. I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, I don’t want to mess this up.”

While she admitted that these emotions might have worked for her character, they were not so good for her state of mind: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there’s so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out—so many—stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”

The turning point came when Holland stepped behind the scenes to encourage her. “It helped that Tom came to set that day, and he was, like, in the corner like, ‘You got this, you’re doing good.’” It was a team effort.

Zendaya and Holland are one of Hollywood’s most admired couples, not only for their discretion (they quietly married last August 4 in Surrey) but also for the care with which they address sensitive issues, such as mental health. Even in the cult series Euphoria, Zendaya’s character, Rue, grapples with psychological issues—in addition to addiction—as a way to raise public awareness and combat the stigma that often surrounds these kinds of situations.

Originally published in Vanity Fair Italia.

#3581. GTA 6 Isn’t Worth Buying A Fancy Controller For

In all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto VI (check out our 10/10 review), it might be tempting to upgrade your setup. For a game 13 years in the making, is now the time to upgrade my TV? Maybe a PS5 Pro is in order? It's a coincidence I finally upgraded my speaker system after 18 years, I swear.

One cheaper upgrade than those above you might be considering is a better controller, like a DualSense Edge or Xbox Elite controller. For all of their myriad upgrades, the most essential reason to ever buy one of these, in my opinion, is for the back paddles. Although they are not technically extra buttons, the ability to map an inconveniently placed button to one of them can make an experience far smoother. 

Some games make an exceptionally strong case for only playing with paddles. You do a lot of sprinting and picking things up in Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, and having to take my thumb off the right stick (thus temporarily locking the camera in place) is something I find to be a constant annoyance. It's such an improvement to be able to do those things while keeping my thumbs where they belong.

Grand Theft Auto VI, on the other hand, is not such an example. Rockstar has finally made a change to the default control scheme it uses in its games, mapping sprint to a click of the left stick, rather than the traditional usage of the X (PlayStation) and A (Xbox) buttons. That alone alleviates a potential argument for needing back paddles (at least as much as one can need such a thing).

That's not to say there's literally zero use for one of these pro-style controllers in GTA 6. In our experience, tapping a paddle is arguably still an improvement to clicking the left stick to sprint or holding L1/LB to bring up the weapon wheel. Enabling Focus Mode is done by clicking both sticks, which you might find awkward; accomplishing that with paddles might be comfortable for you.

GTA 6 doesn't allow its controls to be freely remapped, though there are some options available (such as reverting to that previous style of sprinting). So while there are some reasons you may want to set up the paddles of your pro controller before diving into GTA, it's safe to say that buying one just for this game ain't worth it.

The last time I saw Jared Padalecki, he was – here come some The Boys spoilers – brutally running through and killing people as Mister Marathon. The next time I saw him, he was playing an actor in a wholesome Netflix rom-com on the 2026 Christmas movie schedule. Talk about range. Seriously, I don’t think you can get something more different from a holiday romance than The Boys. So, when I spoke to Padalecki about his new rom-com, Guarding Stars, I asked what it was like jumping between the two projects.

When I was chatting with Padalecki about his book-to-screen adaptation of Katherine Center’s rom-com The Bodyguard, I also mentioned that the last time I saw him was for the Supernatural reunion on The Boys. He immediately cut in to say that the two projects are “very different,” and when I asked him what it was like to jump from one to the other, he explained:

That is weird. It was weird. It was also weird jumping into The Boys in the first place. You know, I'd seen every episode of the show that was out, but I knew I'd be there with [Eric] Kripke and Phil Sgriccia and [Jensen] Ackles and Misha [Collins]. So that was fun.

What’s funny is Jensen Ackles also described this reunion as “weird.” Anyway, getting to Padalecki’s comments, he told me that when it came to The Boys, he wasn’t exactly telling his parents or children to use their Amazon Prime subscription to see it. It was gory and wild, so yeah, that left him saying:

It was one of those things also where I was like telling my mom and dad like, ‘Maybe don't watch this yet’ or like ‘Maybe don't watch it with any people under the age of 21 or 18 or whatever.’ But it was fun.

Well, considering this reunion was called “one of the most fun and bloodiest hours in all of 2026 TV,” I can see why Padalecki wasn’t exactly recommending it to children. However, he had a blast, and when it came time to flip the switch from blood, gore and grossness to wholesome Christmas and romance, it wasn’t a problem. He might have Supernatural to thank for that, as the actor explained:

Every character is, for me, its own kind of entity. You know, I mean, even on Supernatural, I played 20 different versions of Sam, including playing Jared Paddleleki, you know? So I had some experience bouncing around between different versions of whatever my face looks like. But I enjoyed it, actually.

I would imagine that going from playing a wild superhero in maybe the crudest show on TV to working on a Christmas movie that’s made for families would be very fun. You’d get the best of both worlds in a lot of ways, and while whiplash may have been involved, jumping from one production to the other was great for Padalecki.

He also told me that Guarding Stars, which is a project on the 2026 movie schedule that sees him play an actor opposite Leighton Meester’s bodyguard as they decide they need to fake date, served as a nice palate cleanser, or shower, if you will:

After finishing an episode of The Boys, you really want to take a shower and, like, get rid of it, especially the way you know my character ended in The Boys, literally. But this movie was feel-good. You went there, and you're like, ‘I'm gonna watch this with my kids and grandparents or whatever.’

I mean, Jared Padalecki did, as he said, literally have to take a shower after The Boys; he was covered in so much blood after all was said and done. Going to do a Christmas movie afterward helped metaphorically cleanse him too.

As I mentioned, in Guarding Stars, Padalecki plays an actor, Jack, who has to work with a bodyguard, who is played by Leighton Meester. They decide to fake date in an effort to keep her cover, and obviously, as these rom-coms go, cute shenanigans ensue, wholesome family moments happen, and real romantic feelings develop. It’s adorable!

Now, "adorable" is not an adjective you’d use to describe The Boys, so I can see why Jared Padalecki thought it was “weird” to jump between the two projects.

Now, if you’d like to see him drenched in blood, you can stream The Boys on Amazon Prime. If you want to see him falling head over heels for his bodyguard, you can catch Guarding Stars on Netflix starting November 18.

#3579. Texas Teacher Aide Arrested for Allegedly Sexually Assaulting Student

A charter school teacher aide in San Antonio, Texas, was arrested after she was accused of sexually assaulting a student.

Charlyann Silva Guerra was arrested on Wednesday, November 18, charged with one count of sexual assault of child and one count of improper relationship between educator and student, according to Bexar County jail record viewed by Us. Silva Guerra, 26, is currently held on a combined $150,000 bond.

The San Antonio Police Department learned of the allegations against Silva Guerra on Tuesday, November 17, when the school contacted authorities regarding an allegedly improper relationship between Silva Guerra and a female student, according to an arrest affidavit obtained by KSAT.

The affidavit confirmed that Silva Guerra worked at a school, though it did not list the school’s name. However, a School of Science and Technology (SST) Hill Country spokesperson has since confirmed to the outlet that Silva Guerra had been employed with the school since August.

Officers arrived at the school after they received the report, and the student’s mother told them that she found alleged Snapchat messages between her daughter and the teacher aide that were “sexual in nature.”

Silva Guerra also worked as the girl’s basketball coach, according to the affidavit.

The victim’s mother told officers that she also found her daughter and Silva Guerra talking over FaceTime in the middle of the night, which made her suspicious of their relationship.

Officers later interviewed the teen, who allegedly admitted that she and Silva Guerra had engaged in intimate acts just five days before the teacher’s aide was arrested.

Once officers gathered sufficient evidence, Silva Guerra was arrested on the two charges.

Anna Ruiz, marketing and communications coordinator for the school, told KSAT that the district immediately took action once they learned of the allegations.

“The district terminated the employee’s contract and promptly contacted law enforcement officials to ensure the matter was properly addressed and investigated,” Ruiz said. “The safety, well-being, and protection of our students remain our highest priorities. We take all reports of potential misconduct seriously and are committed to cooperating with the appropriate authorities.”

It’s not currently clear if Silva Guerra has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following her arrest. The San Antonio Police Department had no additional updates to share when contacted by Us about the case.

#3577. GTA 6 Finally Changed The Default Rockstar-Game Controls

If you've played Rockstar series like Grand Theft Auto or Read Dead Redemption over the past few decades, then you're familiar with their default control scheme, which maps sprinting to a face button instead of the left analog stick. But Grand Theft Auto VI isn't being hailed as a revolutionary game for nothing--at long last, the default scheme has changed.

As we learned while playing Grand Theft Auto VI, instead of the default setup mapping sprint to a button (A on Xbox and X on PS5), the game maps it to the left analog stick. However, you're free to switch it back to the style used in games like Red Dead Redemption 2, if you prefer.

This is a very handy change, because mapping sprinting to a face button effectively stops you from being able to easily do some of your other actions, unless you have no dignity like me and will use your own face to press a button when your hands are full.

The new default control scheme is far from the most impressive thing in Grand Theft Auto 6, of course. The game earned a rare 10/10 in our GTA 6 review, with Tamoor Hussain calling it "the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach."

For more on the game, check out our ever-expanding GTA 6 guides hub and learn what you should do first. That shouldn't include buying a whole new pro controller, however.

When it comes to celebrity nicknames, is there any better than “JLo”? Jennifer Lopez’s moniker has been synonymous with her storied career for years. It’s been used in her music, it's her social media handle and has been used to name her fashion, fragrance and skincare lines. Although I just found out about how it started. Honestly, I’m so surprised this wasn’t common knowledge to me until today.

JLo has been JLo for over two decades. When the pop star, actress and businesswoman was recently asked about how she got it, here’s what she said:

Heavy D… Sony had Sony Studios down in Manhattan and everybody used to record in there. You could see all the Sony artists in there. And, Heavy would be in there, and he came by one day and I was recording, and I think I was recording my second album, the JLo album. And, I hadn’t named it the JLo album yet. And he came in and he was like, ‘What’s up Jenny Lo? JLo’s in the house.’ He just started calling me that, and I was like, ‘I think I’m gonna name my album JLo’.

Heavy D was a Jamaican-American rapper who had hits such as “Now That We Found Love”, “Got Me Waiting” and “We Got Our Own Thang” in the late 1980s and early 1990s. The rapper tragically died at the age of 44 of a pulmonary embolism back in 2011. As JLo recalled, Heavy D wasn’t only the first person to give her the nickname, it also inspired her to name her second album, J.Lo. When talking about the origin of the name, she also added this:

I never expected it to stick the way it did. I just thought I was going to name the album JLo. And also, [rappers] started putting me in songs as Jennifer Lo, JLo, Jenny Lo. Like, it was a thing. I was already an actress, and I had already made my first record and that had hit, so now they knew who I was, and relationships that were kind of high profile, and they would write about us.

The JLo album came out back in 2001, and the rest is history; she’s been JLo ever since. Along with the album title itself, Lopez noted that she also started being called the nickname in rap songs like Pitbull’s “Culo,” Jay-Z’s “Lost One”.

As she also mentioned, the nickname also got picked up when it came to tabloids writing about her famed relationships – like being one half of Bennifer of course. When JLo was married to Ben Affleck, she officially took his last name for a time, but she never stopped being JLo. And I can’t imagine the nickname ever going away for the superstar.

The origins of JLo came up when she was on the Friends Keep Secrets podcast. Lopez is currently promoting her concert special, The JLo Show. The two-hour affair showcases JLo’s final performance at her Las Vegas residency at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace, which happened in March of this year. It's set to premiere on the 2026 TV schedule on November 26 at 8 p.m. on CBS and with a Paramount+ subscription.

The story of JLo's nickname is so random, but that’s why it’s such a good story. Sometimes you never know how one decision might change your whole career, which was the case with Jennifer Lopez and her JLo album.

#3575. McDonald’s Knows You Won’t Want To Pause GTA 6 To Make Dinner

Contrary to popular belief, you'll need some nutrients to sustain your Grand Theft Auto 6 sessions this week. That means losing valuable time whipping up a meal or driving to your nearest Cluckin' Bell, but McDonald's in the US is aiming to make refueling easier by teaming up with the instant messaging app Discord.

While the fast-food chain already offers a delivery service via its McDelivery app, you won't need to reach for your smartphone to access it. Instead, you can open the McDonald's activity in Discord--which is available on console--place a McDelivery order on Uber Eats, and go back to GTA 6 while you wait for your order to arrive. Alternatively, you can also play Fast Lane Feast, a Discord-exclusive minigame where you collect burgers and chips while racing for a spot on the leaderboards.

Wait for that knock at the door, grab your grub, stuff your food-hole, and get back to your GTA 6 session after you've washed your hands. Repeat as necessary until either the game or the fast food fills the void inside you.

As the GTA 6 week kicks off across the globe — starting in Middle-earth AKA New Zealand — it looks like multiple brands are looking to get involved in what is shaping up to be a major cultural moment for interactive entertainment. KFC is holding a fake funeral in case you want to use up some of your compassionate leave to attend it and take the day off; The Weather Channel has shared a preview of Leonida's weather system, and Xbox is doing its own thing while not explicitly mentioning GTA 6 due to the marketing deal that PlayStation has with the game.

Another big promotion tonight is with the NBA's Miami Heat, as the team will represent the game with GTA 6-inspired gear and a Vice City-themed court for their match against the Milwaukee Bucks.

#3574. Glenn Close Gets Teary-Eyed as She Finally Gets Her Oscar at the Governors Awards

The day before the Governors Awards, a studio executive who had attended the past few years told me that she often found herself crying at the star-studded gala. The annual awards ceremony, held by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, is often an emotional event, with honorary Oscar statuettes bestowed on influential figures in the film industry. A tribute to Michael J. Fox in 2022 and a posthumous honor for Quincy Jones in 2024 left many guests misty-eyed.

At Sunday’s gala, that teary-eyed trend continued when Glenn Close finally got to hold her own Oscar, after eight nominations without a win. Others got emotional when Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, the independent producers from Killer Films, were honored for their tireless work making boundary-pushing and challenging movies. And when Floyd Norman, the 91-year-old artist who was the first Black animator to join Walt Disney Animation Studios, thanked his wife and five children, the crowd cheered along with him. Even though honoree Ridley Scott couldn’t attend, he dedicated his award to his late brother Tony Scott in a video message. “It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand,” said Matt Damon in his remarks for Scott, who has been nominated for four Oscars but has never won competitively.

The presentation of honorary Oscars is often a way to correct Academy Award history, recognizing those who have been overlooked but deserve to be honored for their lifetime of dedication to storytelling and film. The Governors Awards ceremony is also a major stop on the Oscar season campaign trail, with a room packed full of stars and filmmakers from the year’s contenders.

This year that meant a surprising number of couple contenders, including Monica Barbaro and Andrew Garfield (who both star in Artificial), Carrie Coon and Tracy Letts (The Liberation), and Zendaya and Tom Holland. Though Zendaya and Holland arrived together and walked through the Ray Dolby Ballroom as a pair, they actually sat at different tables—Zendaya at the Dune table, with Timothée Chalamet and director Denis Villeneuve, and Holland at the Odyssey table, with director Christopher Nolan. Chalamet also made a date night out of the event, bringing Kylie Jenner with him.

The room held a mix of A-list Hollywood stars, like Tom Cruise (in support of Digger), Julianne Moore (The Debut), and Charlize Theron (The Odyssey), and breakout filmmakers of the year, like Obsession’s Curry Barker, La Bola Negra’s Los Javis, and Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman.

Another breakout of the season, La Bola Negra star Guitarricadelafuente, has been busy promoting the film as both an actor and a musician, having written the original song “La Nieve.” I wondered if he was exhausted from doing double duty. “I’m not tired,” he said with a smile, raving that he had enjoyed meeting many of the other songwriters in the race this year.

All four of the presenters who handed the Oscars to the honorees are also in the Oscar race this year. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star Mahershala Ali honored Norman; Wild Horse Nine star John Malkovich honored his Dangerous Liaisons costar Close; Julianne Moore, teaming up with Todd Haynes, honored Vachon and Koffler; and Damon, the star of The Odyssey, honored Scott.

As Close took the stage to accept the award from Malkovich, she wiped tears away from her eyes. The star of films including Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, The Wife, Albert Nobbs, and The Big Chill spoke about being raised in a religious cult and how, in her childhood, animated films were her only escape. She also spoke about being nominated for eight Oscars over her career, insisting that it didn’t phase her not to emerge victorious. “As an outsider, I have never worried about whether I was going to win or not,” she says. “I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room.”

She wrapped up her speech with a strong statement against AI. “The craft of acting and of great storytelling has never been more vital to the existence of our fragile, violent, but capable-of-transcendence species,” she said. “We are not machines. We are flawed. Our imperfections are our salvation.”

Vachon and Koffler have been making indie films through Killer Films since 1995, championing movies like Far From Heaven, Boys Don’t Cry, Kids, Carol, and Still Alice (which won Moore her Academy Award for lead actress). They dedicated their awards to the many people they’d worked with over the years, some of whom were in the room. “We have walked into propellers with you and what has resulted is usually a piece of work that has touched somebody. Sometimes it’s seen by millions of people and sometimes it’s seen by tens of people,” said Vachon. “But our movies came to life and made it to the screen because writers and directors trusted us with their stories and actors knew we were creating an environment that enabled them to give their best performance.”

Many of the honorees spoke about the mentors and industry giants who had helped them along the way. Close said she’d promised her World According to Garp director, George Roy Hill, that she’d thank him if she ever won an Oscar. “I never got the chance to thank the man who put me in my first movie. Now I can,” she said, holding her statuette up high. Scott, the director whose prolific career output includes Thelma & Louise, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, Alien, Blade Runner, and The Martian, told a story in his video message about making his brother star in his very first project, the 1965 short film Boy and Bicycle. “I’m flattered and proud to accept this award, but I also accept it for Tony,” Scott said of his brother, who died in 2012. “His great work would certainly have earned this recognition.”

The Last of Us cast will be saying goodbye to each other and the Clickers soon.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Last of Us is a TV show that has meant a lot to a lot of people, as it has successfully translated the emotional core of the hugely popular video game and built on the complexity of the character relationships. The final season, anticipated to debut in 2027, is sure to be emotional for fans, too. So it’s not at all surprising to hear that the cast is emotional as they get to the end of filming and will have to say goodbye to each other.

An HBO show that got the world talking from the moment it debuted, the post-apocalyptic drama started by following Joel (Pedro Pascal) as he escorted the teenage Ellie (Bella Ramsey) across a devastated United States ravaged by a fungal infection that had turned people into violent creatures. With Season 3 delving deeper into the journey of Joel’s brother, Tommy Miller, actor Gabriel Luna not only has to say goodbye to a character he’ll know much better, but he’ll also be leaving the cast and crew behind after bidding them an emotional farewell. Here’s what he told Entertainment Weekly about the emotions that are already starting to swirl:

Oh man, a lot of emotions are going around. But right now I think we’re all too tired to feel them. [Laughs.] Because it’s just massive. Obviously I can’t give anything away, but people who’ve played the game know the level of the scope of what we’re dealing with here towards the end of the story. I’m so proud of Bella [Ramsey], Kaitlyn [Dever], and Kyriana [Kratter], who’s joined the cast, for being the tip of the spear and shouldering the weight of this production and what it requires from them.

If you played The Last of Us games, you knew that Abby would be seen on the show as a villain after killing Pedro Pascal's Joel. No matter her motivation or the extent of her own trauma, it would be challenging for viewers to understand the actions of someone taking out such a beloved character. And then, the Season 2 finale ended with the focus shifting to Kaitlyn Dever's Abby, who will take center stage in The Last of Us Season 3.

In a world like the one portrayed in The Last of Us, where everything is heightened as you just try to survive and not get killed or infected, emotions understandably run high for the cast helping bring that world to life. And even though Tommy comes in and out of the story, The Terminal List actor can’t help but be impressed by how the Ellie, Abby, and Lev actors are handling everything required of them, as they head closer to the finish line. He went on to say:

The bulk of my work was back in the summer, and then I’d go back and forth and come in for two, three weeks of time, but they’re here every day and doing the lion’s share of the work.

Since the Naughty Dog video game-turned-TV series is a massive production, it sounds like there’s going to be a prolonged series of goodbyes taking place as storylines are wrapped up and actors depart. Gabriel Luna not only has to process the emotion of saying goodbye to his own character and wrapping up a story that he likely feels very connected to after three seasons, but he also has to handle the departure of each of his co-stars. That’s a lot of emotions for the Dexter: Resurrection star, who will probably be exhausted by the time it’s all said and done. He pretty much said just that:

We’re getting to the end of it, and people are starting to wrap, and we’re giving them their flowers, and then they’re heading off, and one by one, the family is dwindling down to just the final few. We’re about to get a welcomed break and respite from what we’ve been doing, and then we have to come back and finish strong after the holiday. We’re so excited for this thing to come out.

I can only imagine the tears that will be flowing and the emotions that will be felt as the final days of the HBO series come to an end, and everyone says their final goodbyes. Fans anxiously anticipating the third season will have to pack their patience pants while waiting for details on when it will officially premiere. In the meantime, the first two seasons of The Last of Us are streaming with an HBO Max subscription.

#3572. “The “F**k Cut”– Resident Evil Movie Has A Version With A Lot More Swearing

Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie includes a lot of swearing, with main character Bryan (Austin Abrams) saying the words "f**k" and "shit" over and over again as he faces a nightmare in Raccoon City. But the film could have had a lot more swearing.

Cregger said in a new interview with Sony for the movie's home release, that, "The whole thing was carpeted with f**ks. You think there's a lot of f**ks in there now? You should have heard the rough cut. It was insane."

Abrams said he isn't sure how many of the swear words were written into the script, saying there was "definitely a lot improvised."

Cregger, who co-wrote the script with Shay Hatten, said the original script indeed had a lot more f**ks in it. "We tried to go in and take as many as we possibly could out of the movie. I think we probably pulled 70%," he said.

Cregger went on to joke that there is a "F**k Cut" of Resident Evil out there.

Similarly, there is a more comedic cut of the movie that exists. Test screenings showed that it was too funny. "So over the course of my testing, I stripped out as much of the jokes as possible,” he said previously.

Cregger was previously in the sketch comedy group Whitest Kids 'U Know and has some fantastic comedy chops. Perhaps one day we'll get to see Cregger's original version of Resident Evil with more swearing and more comedy.

The Resident Evil movie made more than $400 million globally and ranks as the highest-grossing film of Cregger's career and the top-grossing Resident Evil movie ever. Cregger won't come back for a sequel, though. He got a lot of hate from core gamers about his Resident Evil movie, which didn't feature any storylines or characters from the games, and is now pursuing only original movies as a director.

#3570. The GTA 6 Police Don’t Have Equal Response Times For All Crimes

As with all Grand Theft Auto games, in GTA 6, the police will come after you if you commit a crime with witnesses. However, their response time will not always be the same, and you may be able to use this to your advantage, depending on the situation.

As we learned during our time with Grand Theft Auto 6 so far, the police will respond more slowly if you are assaulting a gang hideout. Presumably, this is because the police force believes you're doing them a favor, but regardless, they will still show up if you get into an all-out firefight and make a bunch of noise.

We also found that, for this reason, using silenced weapons is extremely helpful, as the police will only be called if you are spotted or heard committing a crime. Of course, this is GTA, so you're still naturally going to screw up at some point and have a massive wave of police cars after you, but it doesn't need to happen all the time.

For more on GTA 6, including what to do first, you can check out our guides hub. You can also read our full Grand Theft Auto 6 review, which became the latest in a very small list of games to ever receive a 10/10 score.

#3569. Jennifer Lopez's Most Candid Quotes About Divorce From Ben Affleck

Jennifer Lopez has spent the past two years publicly processing her second split from Ben Affleck — and she has not held back about what the experience taught her.

The singer and actress filed for divorce from Affleck in August 2024 after two years of marriage, and the split was finalized in 2025. In the months since, Lopez has opened up across multiple interviews and podcasts about heartbreak, self-reflection and her new “happy era.”

From calling the breakup “disappointing” to describing it as “the best thing that ever happened,” here is a look at everything Lopez has said about her divorce.

Lopez delivered some of her most pointed remarks yet during an appearance on the “Friends Keep Secrets” podcast hosted by Benny Blanco in November 2026.

“It was such a hard, disappointing last situation on every level,” she told Blanco. “On every level, it was so disappointing. I don’t ever want to delve into that.”

The “On the Floor” singer admitted she has historically been “a serial monogamist, one after another, trying to find the thing, hoping that this was it.” Following her divorce from Affleck, she said she sat in her heartbreak and did the internal work. “It changed me. I allowed it to change me.”

Reflecting on her advice for anyone navigating a split — Lopez was previously married to Ojani Noa, Cris Judd and Marc Anthony — she said divorces are “hard” and “disappointing,” but she tries to hold herself to a standard.

“My advice for divorce is my advice for everything, which is, always operate in a way that you’ll feel proud of when you look back,” Lopez said. “I can look back at these situations and be like, even as painful as some of them were — so bad, life-shifting pain and hurt — I can look back and be like, I loved completely. I acted in a way that I’m proud of as a human.”

She added, “That’s my advice for anything, because when you go through hard things like that, it’s easy to kind of be like, ‘F*** this.’ You’re in so much pain, you want to hurt somebody else, or somebody has hurt you so much that you’re like … but you can’t.”

On a June 2026 episode of the “Smartless” podcast, Lopez got candid about hitting a breaking point after the split.

“There comes a point where it’s all so puzzling and wrong. Where you have to sit there. After my last divorce, I just sat there,” Lopez said. “I canceled my tour and I sat there, and I was like, ‘You need f***ing figure yourself out.’”

Lopez told the hosts she had to resist the urge to blame Affleck for the marriage’s collapse. “[I asked], ‘What is going on with you?’ Forget about everybody else. There’s nobody to blame here except yourself in a certain way,” she said. “Not that people don’t behave in a way that’s not great. But, ‘What are you doing? What do you have going on?’ That was a turning point for me.”

The singer said recognizing “patterns” allowed her to revisit her younger self. “Looking at those patterns, I was able to go back to that little girl [I once was] and really look at her. That little girl with the ripped nightgown — I can see her right now. … Dirty feet, walking around barefoot all the f***ing time. And just kind of going like, ‘You did this. You did all of this. Give yourself a little fing something. A little love! Stop looking for love in other things and give it to yourself.’”

Lopez credited her sister Lynda Lopez with urging her to be her own “keeper.” She added, “These are all little pieces. I feel like the journey is little puzzle pieces that you fit in little by little as you sit there with the oat milk and go, ‘It’s me.’”

Lopez expanded on her year of self-reflection during an appearance on Good Morning America in March 2026.

“I took a year off,” she explained, adding that she had to “stop everything” following the split. “I canceled tours. I decided to just be home and sit in what had happened without running away from it through work, through another person through anything. Just sit.”

The Atlas star said she needed to be present for her twins, Max and Emme, whom she shares with Anthony. “I was just at a point where I was like, ‘What is going on with you?’ I couldn’t blame anybody else because I don’t think that’s where the lesson is. And so, I really needed to figure myself out.”

More than a year later, Lopez described herself as being in her “happy era.”

“I feel like for the first time in my life, I’m free. I’m on my own. It feels really good. I didn’t really know what that felt like since I was in my early 20s, and even before that I always had a boyfriend,” she said. “I’ve gotten to the point where I really trust myself and appreciate myself a little bit more.”

As for dating again? “God forbid,” Lopez quipped. “I don’t want to ruin anything. It’s so nice right now. I’m so happy. It’s the best.”

In a September 2025 interview with CBS Sunday Morning, Lopez credited Affleck’s production company, Artists Equity, with helping bring her film Kiss of the Spider Woman to the screen — and then opened up about the contrast between her set life and home life.

“It was hard not to think about stuff, but it was, like, the best and the worst of times. Every moment on set … I was so happy. And then … back home, it was not great,” Lopez shared. “But you get through it and, you know, honestly, I have to say, it was the best thing that ever happened to me because it changed me. It helped me grow in a way that I needed to grow … become more self-aware. I’m a different person now than I was last year.”

Lopez called the summer following the divorce “probably the best summer I’ve ever had,” adding, “I realized that joy is in living … and really embracing life and everything that it brings to you. The hard times are the lessons and you have to understand that.”

Lopez first broke her silence on the divorce in an October 2024 cover story for Interview magazine with comedian Nikki Glaser.

“I think my whole life I’ve just been trying to say I’m good enough, until where I am now, when I know. I’m giving myself credit. I’m telling that little girl that grew up in the Bronx, ‘You’ve done really good for yourself,’” Lopez told Glaser. She acknowledged that after her recent projects, “my whole f***ing world exploded.”

Rather than searching for another partner, Lopez said she felt energized by independence. “Yes, I’m not looking for anybody, because everything that I’ve done over the past 25, 30 years, being in these different challenging situations, what can I f***ing do when it’s just me flying on my own — What if I’m just free?”

#3568. Lil’ Kim Takes The Spotlight—With A Symphony

When you hear the name Lil’ Kim, a variety of images come to mind. She’s forever known as the force of nature from Brooklyn who turned the music industry on its head when she entered the scene, and her bodacious lyrics and unique fashion sense have kept her as a source of inspiration on your favorite designer’s mood board ever since. On November 18 and 19, to celebrate the music that cemented her icon status, Lil’ Kim will perform in front of a symphony orchestra at the Kings Theatre in Brooklyn, not far from her humble beginnings.

Today she’s less interested in being in the spotlight and more focused on raising her 12-year-old daughter, Royal Reign. In between practices for her performances, Lil’ Kim spoke with Vanity Fair to reflect on her career, how she spends her days, and her standout looks.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: What do you remember about putting your debut album, Hard Core, together?

Lil’ Kim: I remember Biggie and Un [Lance Rivera], who was the label owner that we had. I watched Un build a record label called Undeas, which [stood] for “Un ideas,” and then he finally sold it to Atlantic Records. At the time, we didn’t know the process, but we became Undeas-Atlantic. I remember Biggie having the idea of how he wanted my album to be red, and he explained it to me and Un. I was able to write according to how his idea was to present me, because when they met me, I was who I was—in high heels, jeans, motorcycle jackets, and furs at 13.

Portrait of members of R&B group 112 and rappers Notorious BIG and Lil’ Kim circa 1996

That’s incredible. It sounds like your fashion-icon status started very early. Was there anyone that you looked to back then? What inspired you to dress that way?

My mom was a big inspiration to me when it came to fashion, and so I looked to her for a lot of things. I used to wear her mink coat. She used to wear big sunglasses with her fur coats, with the diamonds and jewelry. She was always taking vacations and I would see her pack her stuff, and she would always have the cutest outfits. They were all matchy-matchy. It’s funny because she would have her outfit to go play tennis in and her outfit would match her tennis racket. So when I bought my big house, I bought a Chanel tennis outfit and I bought the racket to match it, because of my mom.

I love that. Do you keep up with tennis or specifically the ladies in tennis?

No, I haven’t in a while, but, of course, you know, Serena and Venus were like my heroes.

Well, maybe we need to see you on the court one day.

I know. I’m pretty sure I’m rusty, but I like to get out there, though. I used to beat my cousin’s butt back then.

How did the symphony performances come about?

My agents called me and they’re like, “Kim, what do you think?” And I was like, “That’s a freaking awesome idea.” I love performing with bands. And so I imagine that it could be very similar, if not very close. And I thought this could be something really different for me. Sometimes I even listen to classical music. I don’t have to know who the artist is, but I just put on a station and let it flow.

Do you have a favorite song from Hard Core?

I love “Queen Bitch”; it’s my favorite song. It’s still my favorite to perform. And “Crush on You.”

Salma Hayek, Donatella Versace, Pamela Anderson, and Lil’ Kim at Versace’s spring/summer 2001 fashion show

When it comes to fashion, you’re obviously on everyone’s mood board, from stylists to designers, so how important was fashion for you as part of the Lil’ Kim persona?

I just was being myself, honestly. When I first met Biggie, I was coming from my after-school job at Bloomingdale’s. I was probably 13 or 14 at the time, and they would let the teenagers work there.

But I had on a motorcycle jacket and high heels. And one of my best friends told Biggie, “You know, my girl can rap,” because we knew he was rapping around the way. And he was like, “I heard you can rap.” And I just laughed. He was like, “Yeah, see, I knew you didn’t know how to rap.” He was very condescending. He knew how to get you to do what you wanted to do, because I was really shy.

And then I started rapping, and he was blown away because I had on high heels. No one had ever seen someone just bust a rap in high heels. When Biggie, Un, and Jacob York started really talking to me, they didn’t want to change me because that was just what they were so blown away about. That was just who I was.

Do you think people ever misunderstood the way you presented yourself?

To be honest, I never really felt misunderstood by my hardcore fans—the kids my age and the younger kids, they totally got it. I think that’s why I had such a cult following and there was such pandemonium about me when I came out. They understood me. I think it was the older people and the politicians, those are the people who I think misunderstood me.

What did you think of the midterm elections and all of the women who broke barriers in the Senate and gubernatorial offices?

I’m going to be honest with you, I stay away from politics.

Are you keeping up with all of the changes within fashion today? When I listen to your music, you’ve mentioned so many designers and houses, and since then the creative directors have changed. Are you following all of the changes within fashion and seeing how you’re still a part of the conversation?

That’s what I’m trying to say. As a fashion icon, if you really her, and I’m considering myself really her, that’s never gonna change. That’s never going to change. I might put on a fur coat that my stylist or myself will get asked about, because I style myself a lot. And I was styling myself then.

Lil’ Kim and daughter, Royal Reign, on June 16, 2016, in New York City

Extremely rewarding. My daughter’s with me all the time. This world is so cruel and so evil; it’s so different. She’s my safe haven. I feel the extra need to keep her safe.

What does a regular day look like for you?

Lately, I’ve just been really getting into myself. I get up and go have a little spa day. I might take my daughter to go do whatever she wants.

Singer Mary J. Blige with Diana Ross and Lil’ Kim at the 1999 MTV Video Music Awards on September 9, 1999

How do you feel that we’re still talking about your MTV VMAs look in 1999?

I think it’s iconic and I love it. I love when they bring that up, because it was a fun day and it was so good to see people’s faces when they saw my outfit.

Are there any other looks that don’t get as much love as you wish that they did?

I don’t know, because most of the looks that I love, they get the love. There’s a look when I was on the cover of Nylon magazine and I had the teddy bear dress on; that’s one of my favorite looks. The Louis Vuitton look is one of my favorite looks; I love that look. A lot of the Chanel looks and the Versace and the Chanel in the hair.

#3567. Here Are The Most Nominated Games And Publishers At The Game Awards This Year

The nominees for 2026's The Game Awards have been announced, but which games and publishers scored the most total nominations?

The most-nominated game this year Grand Theft Auto 6, which picked up eight total nominations, including a nod for Game of the Year. The game being nominated at all surprised some people considering that it's not even out yet, but members of the voting jury had played it already.

In terms of the most-nominated publishers, Nintendo led the way with a dozen, followed by Capcom with 11 and Annapurna and PlayStation with nine each.

The Game Awards take place on Thursday, December 10. In addition to handing out awards, the show will include game announcements and new trailers. Specifically, Disney has teased some "major" announcements for the event.

Most-Nominated Games

  • Grand Theft Auto 6 - 8
  • Control Resonant, Resident Evil Requiem - 6
  • Phantom Blade Zero - 5
  • Big Walk, 007 First Light, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time - 4
  • Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, Gears of War: E-Day - 3

Most-Nominated Publishers

  • Nintendo - 12
  • Capcom - 11
  • Annapurna, PlayStation - 9
  • Rockstar Games, Xbox - 8
  • Bandai Namco - 7
  • Remedy - 6
  • S-Game - 5
  • CD Projekt Red, IO Interactive, Panic, Square Enix - 4

Disclosure: GameSpot is part of The Game Awards voting jury.

Prince Harry, Meghan Markle and their two kids, Archie and Lilibet, have been adapting to a completely new life in the U.K. these past few months. However, some recent reports claim the family may already be getting ready to head back to Southern California to spend Christmas this year. That leads to the question: Why aren’t they allegedly starting new traditions across the pond?

The Royal Family famously spends their Christmas holiday at the Sandringham Estate in Norfolk. However, while Prince Harry may have grown up doing Christmas at the countryside property, he and Meghan only spent two holidays there – a month after they got engaged in 2017 and their first Christmas as a married couple in 2018. New claims by InStyle speculate that since they broke the tradition eight years ago, they aren't expecting this year to be any different despite the geographical convenience.

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle spent their first two Christmas holidays with the Royal Family at Sandringham Estate. When that time of year rolled around in 2019, they had already formally separated from the Royal Family and appeared in a candid documentary interview where Harry said he and Prince Williams were "on different paths." So in 2019, they decided to spend the holidays privately in Canada with a nine-month-old Archie. And, in March 2020, they stepped away from being senior royals.

It’s expected that Harry and Meghan will share a more intimate holiday season with Meghan’s mother, Doria Ragland, as they usually do. While it’s been suggested they’d likely end the year in the U.S. (via People), a source with the Daily Mail reports Doria may be the one to head to the U.K. instead. Nothing’s been confirmed, but another reason why they aren’t going to the Sandringham Estate could be because they are simply not invited, per an October report:

They know it would be too awkward and too difficult [to spend Christmas with the royal family]. They also know they’re not going to be invited, and they’re not waiting for an invitation.

It's also worth taking into account that Meghan Markle and her mother have been reportedly leaning on each other following Markle’s father facing allegations of possessing child sexual abuse material. Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested by federal agents on November 6 and could serve prison time.

Over in the U.K., the couple reportedly haven’t found their forever home yet since relocating in August. They are currently living at a friend’s private estate in the Cotswolds. Perhaps they are searching for familiarity this holiday season after the big move?

In a 2025 email sent to followers of her lifestyle brand, As Ever, Markle said she was planning on spending the holiday that year with “pajamas all day, some Scrabble or Sequence (or Candyland for the kids), music playing, candles flickering, dogs snoring, endless grazing; the laughter, the sidebars, the deep breaths (you know the ones), the fun, and the memories.” The Royal Family’s Christmas traditions, on the other hand, involve a black-tie dinner and attending service at St Mary Magdalene Church on Christmas morning.

Markle has shared her love of Christmas before, calling it her favorite holiday and even making a special called With Love, Meghan: Holiday Celebration, which you can stream now with a Netflix subscription. Juggling the holidays is rarely easy, even for a power couple like those two.

#3565. Rockstar Founder Issues Rare Statement As GTA 6 Launches To Superb Reviews And Huge Sales

We might not hear from him much, but Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser remains highly involved with the studio and its games, and that includes GTA 6, which is available now in New Zealand and everywhere else on November 19.

To mark the game's launch, Houser released a statement in which he said Rockstar has once again tried to create a game in GTA 6 that "exceeds your expectations" and shows "what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special."

He told GamesRadar: "Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with us."

The executive went on to say that he hopes GTA 6 feels "both familiar and entirely new," and above all else, something that people find to be fun.

"This is a narrative set in a world of possibilities--and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes," he added.

Finally, Houser reminded people that GTA 6 might be the pinnacle of the franchise so far, but Rockstar isn't closing up shop anytime soon.

"We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you," he said.

It's possible it won't be another 13 years for the next GTA game, as Rockstar's owner, Take-Two, has said the "nature and velocity" of GTA releases will change.

Sam Houser rarely releases statements, gives interviews, or appears in Rockstar's promotional efforts, so even this celebratory statement is notable. GQ writer Sam White recently posted a series of tweets (and then deleted them) saying an interview he had planned with Sam Houser fell apart at the last minute.

On GTA 6, Sam Houser was involved in every aspect of the game's creative process.

Sam Houser's brother, Dan Houser, left Rockstar in 2020 after the successful launch of Red Dead Redemption II. He started a new company, Absurd Ventures, which is working on an open-world comedy game that will be revealed soon.

GTA 6 arrives for everyone on November 19, and it's expected to be a massive success, the likes of which the industry hasn't seen since ... 2013's GTA 5. In GameSpot's GTA 6 review, Tamoor Hussain said there might not be another game like it until the inevitable GTA 7.

#3563. How Long Does It Take To Fly Across The Entire GTA 6 Map?

The Grand Theft Auto 6 map is absolutely massive, gigantic, and at least one more synonym to encapsulate its size accurately. Whether it's land, sea, or air, covering it is going to take a lot of time, but just how many hours should you set aside for a flight across Leonida?

We found out for ourselves by piloting a single-propeller plane across the map, which took us an entire four minutes and 10 seconds between the two points on the map. That's pretty big!

We've known for a while that the GTA 6 map was going to be big--with roughly more playable space than GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined--but even that claim doesn't put into perspective just how enormous the game truly is until you experience it for yourself. Another fascinating tidbit is that escaping GTA 6 is nigh-impossible, but definitely worth attempting.

As one streamer has discovered, if you try to cheese it on water using a jet ski, you'll run out of fuel and be left stranded in the water. There might be a happy ending to this scenario, as some streamers have posted clips of a dog on a wave runner coming to their rescue. We've tried to replicate this ourselves, but we've had no luck yet.

But if you choose to stay within Leonida's invisible boundaries, you won't run out of things to do for quite some time. Between missions to improve your lot in life, pursue relationship goals, and soak up the scenery, the reactive open world of GTA 6 will keep you entertained for hours. Our GTA 6 review gave the game a rare 10/10 score, and dozens of other reviewers worldwide have also been very impressed with what Rockstar Games has achieved.

You can experience all of that for yourself soon, and if you're not planning to do some digital tourism with a long walk, check out our GTA 6 guides hub for all kinds of walkthroughs to help you survive and thrive in the game.
